title.zh: 卷二百五十二 列傳第一百四十 楊嗣昌 吳甡
title.en: Volume 252 Biographies 140: Yang Sichang, Wu Shen
title.raw: 卷二百五十二 列傳第一百四十 楊嗣昌 吳甡 Volume 252 Biographies 140: Yang Sichang, Wu Shen

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌吳甡

translations.literal: Yang Sichang, Wu Shen
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang and Wu Shen

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌，字文弱，武陵人。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang, styled Wenruo, was a native of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang, whose courtesy name was Wenruo, came from Wuling.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign (1610).

sentences.zh: 改除杭州府教授。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed professor at Hangzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as a professor in the Hangzhou prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 遷南京國子監博士，累進戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a lecturer at the Nanjing Directorate of Education, and was repeatedly promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to a lectureship at the Nanjing Directorate of Education and rose through successive promotions to bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，引疾歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, citing illness, he retired home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起河南副使，加右參政，移霸州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, he was recalled as vice commissioner of Henan, given the additional title of right assistant commissioner, and transferred to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen (1628) he was recalled to serve as vice commissioner in Henan, promoted to right assistant commissioner, and transferred to Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，移山海關飭兵備。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to regulate military preparations at Shanhai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was reassigned to oversee military defenses at Shanhai Pass.

sentences.zh: 父鶴，總督陜西被逮，嗣昌三疏請代，得減死。

translations.literal: His father He, while grand coordinator of Shaanxi, was arrested; Sichang submitted three memorials asking to take his place, and thus obtained a reduction from the death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Yang He, then grand coordinator of Shaanxi, was arrested, Sichang submitted three memorials offering to serve in his father's stead and won a commutation of the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，擢右僉都御史，巡撫永平、山海諸處。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year, he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Yongping and the Shanhai region.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year (1632) he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Yongping and the surrounding frontier districts including Shanhai.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌父子不附奄，無嫌於東林。

translations.literal: Father and son Sichang did not attach themselves to the eunuchs and had no quarrel with the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Yang Sichang nor his father had sided with the eunuch faction, and they bore no animosity toward the Donglin scholars.

sentences.zh: 侍郎遷安郭鞏以逆案謫戍廣西，其鄉人為訟冤。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Guo Gong of Qian'an, banished to Guangxi on a treason case, had his fellow townsmen plead his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister Guo Gong of Qian'an, having been exiled to Guangxi in connection with a treason case, found his fellow townspeople petitioning on his behalf to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌以部民故，聞於朝，給事中姚思孝駁之，自是與東林郤。

translations.literal: Because Sichang was a fellow townsman, he brought the matter to court attention; the supervising secretary Yao Sixiao objected, and from this time he was at odds with the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: As a fellow native of the region, Sichang raised the case at court; the supervising secretary Yao Sixiao rebuffed him, and from that point he fell out with the Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，拜兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year, he was appointed vice minister of War with the concurrent title of right assistant censor-in-chief, as supreme commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year he was made vice minister of War and right assistant censor-in-chief, with overall command of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 時中原饑，群盜蜂起，嗣昌請開金銀銅錫礦，以解散其黨。

translations.literal: At this time the Central Plains suffered famine and bandits rose everywhere; Sichang requested opening gold, silver, copper, and tin mines to disperse their bands.
translations.idiomatic: With famine afflicting the Central Plains and rebel bands swelling everywhere, Sichang proposed opening mines for gold, silver, copper, and tin so that the disaffected might be dispersed into lawful employment.

sentences.zh: 又六疏陳邊事，多所規畫。

translations.literal: He also submitted six memorials on frontier affairs, offering many plans.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted six further memorials on frontier defense, setting out extensive plans.

sentences.zh: 帝異其才。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his ability.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his talent.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去，復遭繼母喪。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his father's mourning, then again suffered his stepmother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his father, then was overtaken by mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，兵部尚書張鳳翼卒，帝顧廷臣無可任者，即家起嗣昌。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year, Minister of War Zhang Fengyi died; the emperor looked among court officials and found none fit to appoint, and summoned Sichang from home.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Zhang Fengyi died in the autumn of the ninth year (1636), the emperor, finding no suitable minister at court, recalled Sichang directly from his home.

sentences.zh: 三疏辭，不許。

translations.literal: Three times he memorialized to decline; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times by memorial; the emperor would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 明年三月抵京，召對。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he reached the capital and was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Beijing in the third month of the following year and was granted a private audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌通籍後，積歲林居，博涉文籍，多識先朝故事，工筆劄，有口辨。

translations.literal: After entering the registers, Sichang spent years living in retirement, broadly reading literary works, knowing much of former-court precedents, skilled in documents, and gifted in speech.
translations.idiomatic: After taking office he had spent years in retirement, reading widely and mastering the precedents of earlier reigns; he wrote excellent memorials and was an effective speaker.

sentences.zh: 帝與語，大信愛之。

translations.literal: When the emperor spoke with him, he greatly trusted and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation with him the emperor came to trust and favor him deeply.

sentences.zh: 鳳翼故柔靡，兵事無所區畫。

translations.literal: Fengyi had been soft and ineffectual, making no plans for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fengyi had been passive and weak, with no coherent military policy.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌銳意振刷，帝益以為能。

translations.literal: Sichang was bent on vigorous reform; the emperor increasingly regarded him as capable.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang threw himself into revitalizing the military establishment, and the emperor grew ever more convinced of his ability.

sentences.zh: 每對必移時，所奏請無不聽，曰：「恨用卿晚。」

translations.literal: Every audience lasted long; whatever he requested was granted; [the emperor] said: "I regret employing you so late."
translations.idiomatic: Each audience ran long, and every request he made was granted. The emperor said, "I regret having put you to use so late."

sentences.zh: 嗣昌乃議大舉平賊。

translations.literal: Sichang then proposed a major campaign to pacify the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: With that, Sichang proposed a full-scale campaign to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 請以陜西、河南、湖廣、江北為四正，四巡撫分剿而專防；

translations.literal: He requested treating Shaanxi, Henan, Huguang, and Jiangbei as the four "cardinals," with four grand coordinators dividing pursuit while specializing in defense;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed designating Shaanxi, Henan, Huguang, and Jiangbei as the four cardinal regions, each with a grand coordinator assigned to pursuit while focusing chiefly on defense;

sentences.zh: 以延綏、山西、山東、江南、江西、四川為六隅，六巡撫分防而協剿；

translations.literal: Yan-sui, Shanxi, Shandong, Jiangnan, Jiangxi, and Sichuan as the six "corners," with six grand coordinators dividing defense while coordinating pursuit;
translations.idiomatic: and Yan-sui, Shanxi, Shandong, Jiangnan, Jiangxi, and Sichuan as the six corner regions, whose grand coordinators would hold defensive lines while coordinating pursuit—

sentences.zh: 是謂十面之網。

translations.literal: this was called the "ten-sided net."
translations.idiomatic: a scheme known as the "ten-sided net."

sentences.zh: 而總督、總理二臣，隨賊所向，專征討。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the supreme commander and the grand coordinator-general would follow wherever the bandits went and conduct specialized campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the supreme commander and the coordinator-general would follow the rebels wherever they went and lead the main offensive.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫熊文燦者，討海賊有功，大言自詭足辦賊。

translations.literal: The Fujian grand coordinator Xiong Wencan, who had merit in suppressing sea bandits, spoke grandly claiming he was fully able to handle the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wencan, grand coordinator of Fujian, had distinguished himself against pirates on the coast and now boasted that he alone could finish off the rebels.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌聞而善之。

translations.literal: Sichang heard this and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang heard him and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 會總督洪承疇、王家楨分駐陜西、河南。

translations.literal: It happened that supreme commanders Hong Chengchou and Wang Jiazhen were separately stationed in Shaanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the supreme commanders Hong Chengchou and Wang Jiazhen were posted respectively in Shaanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 家楨故庸材，不足任，嗣昌乃薦文燦代之。

translations.literal: Jiazhen was by nature a mediocre talent, inadequate to the task; Sichang therefore recommended Wencan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiazhen was a mediocrity unfit for the role, so Sichang recommended Wencan in his place.

sentences.zh: 因議增兵十二萬，增餉二百八十萬。

translations.literal: He then proposed increasing troops by 120,000 and revenue by 2,800,000.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed raising an additional 120,000 troops and 2.8 million taels in funds.

sentences.zh: 其措餉之策有四，曰因糧，曰溢地，曰事例，曰驛遞。

translations.literal: His methods for raising revenue were four: called "following grain," "surplus land," "precedent cases," and "post relay."
translations.idiomatic: His four revenue measures were called grain surcharges, surplus-land assessment, purchase of office by contribution, and postal savings.

sentences.zh: 因糧者，因舊額之糧，量為加派，畝輸糧六合，石折銀八錢，傷地不與，歲得銀百九十二萬九千有奇；

translations.literal: For "following grain": based on the old grain quota, a proportional surcharge was levied—six he per mu, eight qian of silver per shi, barren land exempted—yielding somewhat more than 1,929,000 taels per year;
translations.idiomatic: The grain surcharge built on existing grain quotas with a proportional levy of six he per mu, converted at eight qian of silver per shi, with barren land exempted, yielding somewhat more than 1,929,000 taels annually;

sentences.zh: 溢地者，民間土田溢原額者，核實輸賦，歲得銀四十萬六千有奇；

translations.literal: For "surplus land": private fields exceeding the original quota were verified and taxed, yielding somewhat more than 406,000 taels per year;
translations.idiomatic: the surplus-land assessment verified and taxed farmland exceeding registered quotas, yielding somewhat more than 406,000 taels annually;

sentences.zh: 事例者，富民輸資為監生，一歲而止；

translations.literal: For "precedent cases": wealthy households paid funds to become student-inspectors, for one year only;
translations.idiomatic: the precedent-case measure allowed wealthy households to buy the status of student-inspector by contribution for a single year;

sentences.zh: 驛遞者，前此郵驛裁省之銀，以二十萬充餉。

translations.literal: For "post relay": silver saved from earlier postal and courier cuts, 200,000 used for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: and postal savings redirected the 200,000 taels cut from the courier system to military funds.

sentences.zh: 議上，帝乃傳諭：「流寇延蔓，生民塗炭，不集兵無以平寇，不增賦無以餉兵。

translations.literal: When the plan was submitted, the emperor issued a transmitted edict: "The roving bandits spread unchecked and the people suffer in misery; without gathering troops the bandits cannot be pacified, without increasing levies the troops cannot be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan reached him, the emperor issued a transmitted edict: "The roving rebels spread unchecked and the people suffer in misery. Without gathering troops the rebels cannot be suppressed, and without increasing levies the troops cannot be supplied.

sentences.zh: 勉從廷議，暫累吾民一年，除此腹心大患。

translations.literal: Reluctantly following court deliberation, temporarily burdening Our people for one year, to remove this grave internal threat.
translations.idiomatic: Reluctantly following the court's deliberation, I shall temporarily burden my people for one year to remove this grave internal threat.

sentences.zh: 其改因糧為均輸，布告天下，使知為民去害之意。」

translations.literal: Change the name from 'following grain' to 'equal transport,' proclaim it throughout the realm, so all may know the intent to remove harm for the people."
translations.idiomatic: Rename the grain surcharge as 'equal transport' and proclaim it throughout the realm, so all may know the intent is to remove harm for the people."

sentences.zh: 尋議諸州縣練壯丁捍本土，詔撫按飭行。

translations.literal: Soon he also proposed that all prefectures and counties drill stout youths to defend their native places, and an edict ordered grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners to enforce it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also proposed that every prefecture and county drill able-bodied men to defend their home districts, and an edict ordered the grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners to enforce the measure.

sentences.zh: 賊攻淅川，左良玉不救，城陷。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked Xichuan; Zuo Liangyu did not rescue it, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked Xichuan, Zuo Liangyu failed to relieve it and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 山西總兵王忠援河南，稱疾不進，兵噪而歸。

translations.literal: The Shanxi regional commander Wang Zhong was sent to aid Henan, claimed illness and would not advance, and his troops mutinied and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanxi regional commander Wang Zhong, sent to reinforce Henan, pleaded illness and refused to advance; his troops mutinied and marched home.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌請逮戮失事諸帥，以肅軍令，遂逮忠及故總兵張全昌。

translations.literal: Sichang requested arresting and executing commanders who had failed in duty to stiffen military discipline, and thus Wang Zhong and the former regional commander Zhang Quanchang were arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang requested that commanders who had failed in duty be arrested and punished to stiffen military discipline; Wang Zhong and the former regional commander Zhang Quanchang were accordingly seized.

sentences.zh: 良玉以六安功，落職戴罪自贖。

translations.literal: Liangyu, for his merit at Lu'an, was demoted but allowed to redeem guilt through service.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu, credited with merit at Lu'an, was demoted but allowed to redeem his guilt through further service.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌既建「四正六隅」之說，欲專委重文燦，文燦顧主撫議，與前策牴牾。

translations.literal: Sichang having established the doctrine of "four cardinals and six corners," wished to entrust full weight to Wencan, but Wencan favored pacification by appeasement, contradicting the earlier strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Having devised the "four cardinals and six corners" scheme, Sichang wished to place full authority in Wencan's hands, but Wencan favored appeasement, which contradicted the earlier strategy.

sentences.zh: 帝譙讓文燦，嗣昌亦心望。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Wencan, and Sichang also inwardly hoped [for better results].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Wencan, and Sichang too inwardly hoped for better results.

sentences.zh: 既已任之，則曲為之解，乃上疏曰：「網張十面，必以河南、陜西為殺賊之地。

translations.literal: Having already appointed him, he bent to explain for him, and submitted a memorial saying: "With the net spread on ten sides, Henan and Shaanxi must be the places to destroy the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Having already appointed him, Sichang bent over backward to defend him and submitted a memorial: "With the net spread on ten sides, Henan and Shaanxi must be the places where the rebels are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 然陜有李自成、惠登相等，大部未能剿絕，法當驅關東賊不使合，而使陜撫斷商、雒，鄖撫斷鄖、襄，安撫斷英、六，鳳撫斷亳、潁，而應撫之軍出靈、陜，保撫之軍渡延津。

translations.literal: Yet Shaanxi has Li Zicheng, Hui Dengqi, and others; their great bands cannot yet be exterminated. The method should be to drive the bandits east of the passes so they do not unite, and have the Shaanxi coordinator block Shang and Luo, the Yun coordinator block Yun and Xiang, the Anqing coordinator block Ying and Lu, the Fengyang coordinator block Bo and Ying, while the Ying coordinator's troops advance from Ling and Shaan, and the Baoding coordinator's troops cross Yanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shaanxi still harbors Li Zicheng, Hui Dengqi, and others in bands too large to exterminate at once. The method is to drive the rebels east of the passes before they can unite, while the Shaanxi coordinator blocks Shang and Luo, the Yun coordinator blocks Yun and Xiang, the Anqing coordinator blocks Ying and Lu, the Fengyang coordinator blocks Bo and Ying, the Ying coordinator's troops advance from Ling and Shaan, and the Baoding coordinator's troops cross the Yanjin ford.

sentences.zh: 然後總理提邊兵，監臣提禁旅，豫撫提陳永福諸軍，並力合剿。

translations.literal: Then the coordinator-general leads frontier troops, the supervising minister leads the capital guard, the Henan coordinator leads Chen Yongfu's armies, and all join forces for combined suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Then the coordinator-general leads the frontier troops, the supervising minister leads the capital guard, the Henan coordinator leads Chen Yongfu's forces, and all join in a combined offensive.

sentences.zh: 若關中大賊逸出關東，則秦督提曹變蛟等出關協擊。

translations.literal: If great bandits from within the passes escape east of the passes, then the Qin supreme commander leads Cao Bianjiao and others east of the passes to assist in attack.
translations.idiomatic: If major rebel forces slip east of the passes, the Shaanxi supreme commander will lead Cao Bianjiao and others out of the passes to assist in the attack.

sentences.zh: 期三月盡諸劇寇。

translations.literal: The deadline is three months to eliminate all fierce bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The deadline is three months to eliminate all the major rebel bands.

sentences.zh: 巡撫不用命，立解其兵柄，簡一監司代之；

translations.literal: If a grand coordinator disobeys orders, immediately relieve him of military authority and select one surveillance commissioner to replace him;
translations.idiomatic: If a grand coordinator disobeys orders, immediately relieve him of military authority and appoint a surveillance commissioner in his place;

sentences.zh: 總兵不用命，立奪其帥印，簡一副將代之；

translations.literal: if a regional commander disobeys orders, immediately seize his commander's seal and select one vice commander to replace him;
translations.idiomatic: if a regional commander disobeys orders, immediately seize his commander's seal and appoint a vice commander in his place;

sentences.zh: 監司、副將以下，悉以尚方劍從事。

translations.literal: for surveillance commissioners, vice commanders, and below, all may be dealt with by the imperial sword.
translations.idiomatic: and for surveillance commissioners, vice commanders, and all ranks below, the imperial sword may be applied without further appeal.

sentences.zh: 則人人效力，何賊不平。」

translations.literal: Then every man will exert himself—what bandit could fail to be pacified?"
translations.idiomatic: Then every man will exert himself—what rebel could fail to be suppressed?"

sentences.zh: 乃克今年十二月至明年二月為滅賊之期。

translations.literal: He then fixed from the twelfth month of this year to the second month of next year as the period for destroying the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed the period from the twelfth month of this year to the second month of next as the deadline for destroying the rebels.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 是時，賊大入四川，朝士尤洪承疇縱賊。

translations.literal: At this time the bandits made a major incursion into Sichuan, and court officials especially blamed Hong Chengchou for letting the bandits go.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the rebels made a major incursion into Sichuan, and court officials especially blamed Hong Chengchou for letting them roam free.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌因言於帝曰：「熊文燦在事三月，承疇七年不效。

translations.literal: Sichang therefore said to the emperor: "Xiong Wencan has been in office three months; Chengchou seven years without effect.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang therefore said to the emperor, "Xiong Wencan has been in office three months; Chengchou seven years without effect.

sentences.zh: 論者繩文燦急，而承疇縱寇莫為言。」

translations.literal: Critics press Wencan urgently, yet for Chengchou letting bandits go no one speaks."
translations.idiomatic: Critics press Wencan urgently, yet for Chengchou letting the rebels roam free no one speaks up."

sentences.zh: 帝知嗣昌有意左右之，變色曰：「督、理二臣但責成及時平賊，奈何以久近藉之口！」

translations.literal: The emperor knew Sichang intended to favor one side, changed color and said: "The supreme commander and coordinator-general are only charged to pacify the bandits in time—how can you use length of service as a pretext!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing that Sichang meant to favor one side, flushed and said, "The supreme commander and coordinator-general are charged only to pacify the rebels in good time—how dare you use length of service as a pretext!"

sentences.zh: 嗣昌乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Sichang then dared not speak further.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang then dared not speak further.

sentences.zh: 文燦既主撫議，所加餉天子遣一侍郎督之，本藉以剿賊，文燦悉以資撫。

translations.literal: Wencan having favored appeasement, the added funds the Son of Heaven sent a vice minister to supervise were originally meant for suppression; Wencan used them all for appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan having favored appeasement, the added funds that the emperor sent a vice minister to supervise were originally meant for military suppression; Wencan spent them all on appeasement instead.

sentences.zh: 帝既不復詰，廷臣亦莫言之。

translations.literal: The emperor no longer questioned it, and court officials also did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor no longer questioned the matter, and no court official spoke of it either.

sentences.zh: 至明年三月，嗣昌以滅賊逾期，疏引罪，薦人自代。

translations.literal: By the third month of the following year, Sichang, because destroying the bandits had passed the deadline, submitted a memorial accepting guilt and recommending someone to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: By the third month of the following year, with the deadline for destroying the rebels past, Sichang submitted a memorial accepting guilt and recommending a successor.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，而命察行間功罪，乃上疏曰：「洪承疇專辦秦賊，賊往來秦、蜀自如，剿撫俱無功，不免於罪。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it, but ordered investigation of merits and faults in the field, and [Sichang] submitted a memorial saying: "Hong Chengchou specialized in Shaanxi bandits; the bandits moved freely between Shaanxi and Sichuan; both suppression and appeasement were without effect—he cannot escape guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, but ordered an inquiry into merits and faults in the field. Sichang then submitted a memorial: "Hong Chengchou was charged solely with the Shaanxi rebels, yet they moved freely between Shaanxi and Sichuan; both suppression and appeasement failed—he cannot escape guilt.

sentences.zh: 熊文燦兼辦江北、河南、湖廣賊，撫劉國能、張獻忠，戰舞陽、光山，剿撫俱有功，應免罪。

translations.literal: Xiong Wencan concurrently handled Jiangbei, Henan, and Huguang bandits, appeased Liu Guoneng and Zhang Xianzhong, fought at Wuyang and Guangshan—both suppression and appeasement had merit; he should be exempted from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wencan handled rebels in Jiangbei, Henan, and Huguang together, appeased Liu Guoneng and Zhang Xianzhong, and fought at Wuyang and Guangshan—he achieved results in both suppression and appeasement and should be exempted from guilt.

sentences.zh: 諸巡撫則河南常道立、湖廣余應桂有功，陜西孫傳庭、山西宋賢、山東顏繼祖、保定張其平、江南張國維、江西解學龍、浙江喻思恂有勞，鄖陽戴東旻無功過，鳳陽朱大典、安慶史可法宜策勵圖功。

translations.literal: Among grand coordinators: Henan's Chang Daoli and Huguang's Yu Yinggui had merit; Shaanxi's Sun Chuanting, Shanxi's Song Xian, Shandong's Yan Jizu, Baoding's Zhang Qiping, Jiangnan's Zhang Guowei, Jiangxi's Xie Xuelong, and Zhejiang's Yu Sixun had labor; Yunyang's Dai Dongmin had neither merit nor fault; Fengyang's Zhu Dadian and Anqing's Shi Kefa should be urged to strive for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Among the grand coordinators, Chang Daoli of Henan and Yu Yinggui of Huguang had merit; Sun Chuanting of Shaanxi, Song Xian of Shanxi, Yan Jizu of Shandong, Zhang Qiping of Baoding, Zhang Guowei of Jiangnan, Xie Xuelong of Jiangxi, and Yu Sixun of Zhejiang had done solid work; Dai Dongmin of Yunyang had neither merit nor fault; Zhu Dadian of Fengyang and Shi Kefa of Anqing should be urged to strive for achievement.

sentences.zh: 總兵則河南左良玉有功，陜西曹變蛟、左光先無功，山西虎大威、山東倪寵、江北牟文綬、保定錢中選有勞無功，河南張任學、寧夏祖大弼無功過。

translations.literal: Among regional commanders: Henan's Zuo Liangyu had merit; Shaanxi's Cao Bianjiao and Zuo Guangxian had no merit; Shanxi's Hu Dawei, Shandong's Ni Chong, Jiangbei's Mou Wenshou, and Baoding's Qian Zhongxuan had labor without merit; Henan's Zhang Renxue and Ningxia's Zu Dabi had neither merit nor fault.
translations.idiomatic: Among the regional commanders, Zuo Liangyu of Henan had merit; Cao Bianjiao and Zuo Guangxian of Shaanxi had none; Hu Dawei of Shanxi, Ni Chong of Shandong, Mou Wenshou of Jiangbei, and Qian Zhongxuan of Baoding exerted themselves without success; Zhang Renxue of Henan and Zu Dabi of Ningxia had neither merit nor fault.

sentences.zh: 承疇宜遣逮，因軍民愛戴，請削宮保、尚書，以侍郎行事。

translations.literal: Chengchou should be sent for arrest; because troops and people love and honor him, request stripping him of Grand Guardian and Minister titles, to act as vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou should be sent for arrest; because troops and civilians esteem him, I request stripping him of his Grand Guardian and Minister titles and allowing him to serve as vice minister.

sentences.zh: 變蛟、光先貶五秩，與大弼期五月平賊，逾期並承疇逮治。

translations.literal: Bianjiao and Guangxian demoted five ranks; with Dabi set a deadline of five months to pacify bandits—if overdue, together with Chengchou sent for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao and Guangxian were demoted five ranks; Dabi was given five months to pacify the rebels, with the understanding that if the deadline passed, he and Chengchou would be arrested together.

sentences.zh: 大典貶三秩，可法戴罪自贖。」

translations.literal: Dadian demoted three ranks; Kefa to redeem guilt through service."
translations.idiomatic: Dadian was demoted three ranks; Kefa was allowed to redeem his guilt through further service."

sentences.zh: 議上，帝悉從之。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor followed it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor approved it in full.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌既終右文燦，而文燦實不知兵。

translations.literal: Sichang having ultimately favored Wencan, yet Wencan truly did not understand military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang had ultimately sided with Wencan, yet Wencan truly understood nothing of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 既降國能、獻忠，謂撫必可恃。

translations.literal: Having induced Guoneng and Xianzhong to surrender, he believed appeasement could surely be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Guoneng and Zhang Xianzhong had surrendered, he believed appeasement could surely be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌亦陰主之，所請無不曲徇，自是不復言「十面張網」之策矣。

translations.literal: Sichang also secretly supported him; whatever he requested was bent to comply without exception—from this time he no longer spoke of the "ten-sided net" strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang also secretly supported him; whatever Wencan requested was granted without exception, and from that point Sichang no longer spoke of the "ten-sided net" strategy.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝御經筵畢，嗣昌奏對有「善戰服上刑」等語，帝怫然，詰之曰：「今天下一統，非戰國兵爭比。

translations.literal: That month, when the emperor had finished the classics lecture, Sichang in audience response used phrases such as "those skilled in war submit to the highest punishment"; the emperor was displeased and questioned him: "Today the realm is unified—it is not comparable to the Warring States military contests.
translations.idiomatic: That month, after the emperor's lecture on the classics, Sichang in his audience response used phrases such as "those skilled in war submit to the highest punishment." The emperor was displeased and challenged him: "The realm is unified today—it is not comparable to the military contests of the Warring States period.

sentences.zh: 小醜跳梁，不能伸大司馬九伐之法，奈何為是言？」

translations.literal: Petty villains leap about—cannot extend the Grand Marshal's nine punitive campaigns—why make such words?"
translations.idiomatic: Petty villains leap about, yet you cannot apply the Grand Marshal's nine punitive campaigns—why speak in such terms?"

sentences.zh: 嗣昌慚。

translations.literal: Sichang was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 當是時，流賊既大熾，朝廷又有東顧憂，嗣昌復陰主互市策。

translations.literal: At this time the roving bandits had greatly flared up, and the court also had worries looking east; Sichang again secretly favored a border-trade policy.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the roving rebels had grown fierce, and the court also had worries in the east; Sichang again secretly favored a policy of border trade with the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 適太陰掩熒惑，帝減膳修省，嗣昌則歷引漢永平、唐元和、宋太平興國事，蓋為互市地雲。

translations.literal: It happened that the moon eclipsed Mars; the emperor reduced meals and practiced self-examination; Sichang then cited in succession Han Yongping, Tang Yuanhe, and Song Taiping Xingguo precedents—apparently paving ground for border trade.
translations.idiomatic: When the moon eclipsed Mars, the emperor reduced his meals and practiced self-examination; Sichang then cited in succession precedents from the Han Yongping, Tang Yuanhe, and Song Taiping Xingguo reigns—apparently paving the way for border trade.

sentences.zh: 給事中何楷疏駁之，給事中錢增、御史林蘭友相繼論列，帝不問。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary He Kai memorialized in rebuttal; the supervising secretary Qian Zeng and censor Lin Lanyou successively debated; the emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary He Kai memorialized in rebuttal; the supervising secretary Qian Zeng and the censor Lin Lanyou debated the matter in turn; the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 六月，改禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，入參機務，仍掌兵部事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, he was transferred to Minister of Rites with concurrent appointment as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering to participate in state affairs, while still managing Ministry of War affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the inner cabinet while continuing to direct Ministry of War affairs.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌既以奪情入政府，又奪情起陳新甲總督，於是楷、蘭友及少詹事黃道周抗疏詆斥，修撰劉同升、編修越士春繼之。

translations.literal: Sichang having entered government by seizing mourning obligation, also seized mourning to recall Chen Xinji as supreme commander; thereupon Kai, Lanyou, and junior mentor Huang Daozhou submitted defiant memorials denouncing him; compiler Liu Tongsheng and editor Yue Shichun followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang having entered government without completing mourning for his father, also recalled Chen Xinji as supreme commander without regard to mourning; thereupon Kai, Lanyou, and the junior mentor Huang Daozhou submitted defiant memorials denouncing him, followed by the compiler Liu Tongsheng and the editor Yue Shichun.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，並鐫三級，留翰林。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted all three ranks, retaining them in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted all of them three ranks, retaining them in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事張若麒上疏醜詆道周，遂鐫道周六級，並同升、士春皆謫外。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice clerk Zhang Ruoqi submitted a memorial vilifying Daozhou; Daozhou was then demoted six ranks, and Tongsheng and Shichun were all banished abroad.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice clerk Zhang Ruoqi submitted a memorial vilifying Daozhou; Daozhou was demoted six ranks, and Tongsheng and Shichun were all banished to posts outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 已而南京御史成勇、兵部尚書範景文等言之，亦獲譴。

translations.literal: Soon the Nanjing censor Cheng Yong, Minister of War Fan Jingwen, and others spoke on it and also received reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Nanjing censor Cheng Yong, Minister of War Fan Jingwen, and others spoke up as well and were likewise punished.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌自是益不理於人口。

translations.literal: From this time Sichang was increasingly unacceptable in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Sichang grew ever more unpopular in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 我大清兵入墻子嶺、青口山，薊遼保定總督吳阿衡方醉，不能軍，敗死。

translations.literal: Our Great Qing troops entered Qiangzi Ridge and Qingkou Mountain; the Jizhou-Liaodong-Baoding supreme commander Wu Aheng was drunk and could not command the army, and was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Qing troops entered Qiangzi Ridge and Qingkou Mountain; the Jizhou-Liaodong-Baoding supreme commander Wu Aheng was drunk and unable to command his troops, and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 京城戒嚴，召盧象升帥師入衛。

translations.literal: The capital was placed under martial law; Lu Xiangsheng was summoned to lead troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was placed under martial law, and Lu Xiangsheng was summoned to lead troops to its defense.

sentences.zh: 象升主戰，嗣昌與監督中官高起潛主款，議不合，交惡。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng favored fighting; Sichang and the supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian favored appeasement—their views did not agree and they became mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng favored fighting; Sichang and the supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian favored appeasement. Their views clashed and they became mutually hostile.

sentences.zh: 編修楊廷麟劾嗣昌誤國，嗣昌怒，改廷麟職方主事監象升軍，而戒諸將毋輕戰。

translations.literal: The editor Yang Tinglin impeached Sichang for harming the state; Sichang was angry, transferred Tinglin to Bureau of Operations clerk to supervise Xiangsheng's army, yet warned all generals not to fight lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The editor Yang Tinglin impeached Sichang for harming the state. Sichang in anger transferred Tinglin to a clerkship in the Bureau of Operations to supervise Xiangsheng's army, yet warned all the generals not to engage lightly.

sentences.zh: 諸將本恇怯，率藉口持重觀望，所在列城多破。

translations.literal: The generals were by nature timid and cowardly, all using caution as pretext to watch and wait; walled cities everywhere mostly fell.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were by nature timid and cowardly and all used caution as a pretext to hold back and wait; walled cities fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌據軍中報，請旨授方略。

translations.literal: Sichang based on army reports requested imperial instructions to grant strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang, relying on reports from the army, requested imperial instructions on strategy.

sentences.zh: 比下軍前，則機宜已變，進止乖違，疆事益壞雲。

translations.literal: By the time [orders] reached the army front, the opportune moment had already changed, advance and halt were at odds, and frontier affairs grew worse still.
translations.idiomatic: By the time orders reached the front, the situation had already changed, advance and retreat fell out of step, and frontier affairs grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 象升既陣亡，嗣昌亦貶三秩，戴罪視事。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng having died in battle, Sichang was also demoted three ranks and continued in office bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangsheng fell in battle, Sichang was demoted three ranks as well and continued in office under sentence of guilt.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，濟南告陷，德王被執，遊騎北抵兗州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, Jinan reported fallen; the Prince of De was captured; roaming cavalry reached north to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year (1639), Jinan fell; the Prince of De was captured, and roaming enemy cavalry pushed north as far as Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，大清兵北旋，給事中李希沆言：「聖明禦極以來，北兵三至。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Great Qing troops withdrew north; the supervising secretary Li Xikang said: "Since the sage emperor ascended the throne, northern troops have come three times.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Qing troops withdrew northward, and the supervising secretary Li Xikang said, "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, northern armies have invaded three times.

sentences.zh: 己巳之罪未正，致有丙子；

translations.literal: The crimes of jisi were not rectified, leading to bingzi;
translations.idiomatic: The crimes of the jisi year were never punished, which led to the bingzi invasion;

sentences.zh: 丙子之罪未正，致有今日。」

translations.literal: the crimes of bingzi were not rectified, leading to today."
translations.idiomatic: the crimes of the bingzi year were never punished, which led to today."

sentences.zh: 語侵嗣昌。

translations.literal: The words impinged on Sichang.
translations.idiomatic: His words were aimed at Sichang.

sentences.zh: 御史王誌舉亦劾嗣昌誤國四大罪，請用丁汝夔、袁崇煥故事。

translations.literal: The censor Wang Zhiju also impeached Sichang with four great crimes of harming the state, requesting application of the precedents of Ding Ruokui and Yuan Chonghuan.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Wang Zhiju also impeached Sichang on four counts of harming the state and asked that the precedents of Ding Ruokui and Yuan Chonghuan be applied.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，希沆貶秩，誌舉奪官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Xikang was demoted in rank, Zhiju stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry; Xikang was demoted in rank and Zhiju stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以嗣昌才而用之，非廷臣意，知其必有言，言者輒斥。

translations.literal: Initially the emperor used Sichang for his talent, not as court officials wished; knowing there would surely be criticism, whoever spoke was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had appointed Sichang for his talent against the court's wishes; expecting criticism, he dismissed whoever spoke out.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌既有罪，帝又數逐言官，中外益不平。

translations.literal: Sichang already had guilt, and the emperor again repeatedly expelled remonstrating officials; inside and outside grew more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: With Sichang already in disgrace and the emperor again expelling remonstrating officials, resentment spread through court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌亦不自安，屢疏引罪，乃落職冠帶視事。

translations.literal: Sichang also was ill at ease, repeatedly memorializing to accept guilt, and was then reduced in office but retained cap and belt to conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang grew uneasy as well and repeatedly memorialized to accept guilt; he was reduced in rank but allowed to retain his insignia and continue in office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以敘功復之。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of recording merit, he was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored on account of recorded merit.

sentences.zh: 先是，京師被兵，樞臣皆坐罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the capital suffered military attack, military ministers all bore guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, whenever the capital came under attack, the military ministers had all been punished.

sentences.zh: 二年，王洽下獄死，復論大辟。

translations.literal: In the second year, Wang Qia died in prison, and capital punishment was again debated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Wang Qia died in prison and capital punishment was debated again.

sentences.zh: 九年，張鳳翼出督師，服毒死，猶削籍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Zhang Fengyi went out as supreme commander, took poison and died, yet still had his name struck from registers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Zhang Fengyi went out as supreme commander, took poison and died, yet still had his name struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 及是，亡七十余城，而帝眷嗣昌不衰。

translations.literal: By this time more than seventy cities were lost, yet the emperor's favor toward Sichang did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: By this time more than seventy cities had been lost, yet the emperor's favor toward Sichang did not wane.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌乃薦四川巡撫傅宗龍自代。

translations.literal: Sichang then recommended the Sichuan grand coordinator Fu Zonglong to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang then recommended the Sichuan grand coordinator Fu Zonglong as his successor.

sentences.zh: 帝命嗣昌議文武諸臣失事罪，分五等：曰守邊失機，曰殘破城邑，曰失陷藩封，曰失亡主帥，曰縱敵出塞。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Sichang to deliberate guilt of civil and military officials who failed in duty, divided into five grades: called losing opportunity while guarding the frontier, ravaging and breaking cities and towns, losing princely enfeoffments, losing and destroying commanders, and letting the enemy escape beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Sichang to classify the guilt of civil and military officials who had failed in duty into five grades: losing opportunity while guarding the frontier, ravaging cities and towns, losing princely enfeoffments, losing commanders, and letting the enemy escape beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 於是中官則薊鎮總監鄧希詔、分監孫茂霖，巡撫則順天陳祖苞、保定張其平、山東顏繼祖，總兵則薊鎮吳國俊、陳國威，山東倪寵，援剿祖寬、李重鎮及他副將以下，至州縣有司，凡三十六人，同日棄市。

translations.literal: Thereupon among eunuch officials: Jizhou garrison supervising commissioner Deng Xixu and sub-commissioner Sun Maolin; among grand coordinators: Shuntian Chen Zubao, Baoding Zhang Qiping, Shandong Yan Jizu; among regional commanders: Jizhou Wu Guojun, Chen Guowei, Shandong Ni Chong, relief-suppression Zu Kuan, Li Chongzhen and other vice commanders and below, down to prefecture and county officials—in all thirty-six persons, executed in the market on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Among the eunuch officials, the Jizhou supervising commissioner Deng Xixu and sub-commissioner Sun Maolin were executed; among the grand coordinators, Chen Zubao of Shuntian, Zhang Qiping of Baoding, and Yan Jizu of Shandong; among the regional commanders, Wu Guojun and Chen Guowei of Jizhou, Ni Chong of Shandong, Zu Kuan and Li Chongzhen of the relief forces, and other vice commanders and below down to prefectural and county officials—in all thirty-six men were executed in the market on the same day.

sentences.zh: 而嗣昌貶削不及，物議益嘩。

translations.literal: Yet Sichang's demotion and reduction did not reach him, and public opinion grew more clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sichang himself escaped demotion, and public outrage grew louder.

sentences.zh: 當戒嚴時，廷臣多請練邊兵。

translations.literal: When martial law was declared, court officials mostly requested drilling frontier troops.
translations.idiomatic: When martial law was declared, many court officials urged drilling the frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌因定議：宣府、大同、山西三鎮兵十七萬八千八百有奇，三總兵各練萬，總督練三萬，以二萬駐懷來，一萬駐陽和，東西策應。

translations.literal: Sichang therefore fixed the plan: Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi three garrisons' troops 178,800 odd; three regional commanders each drill 10,000, supreme commander drills 30,000, with 20,000 stationed at Huailai, 10,000 at Yanghe, east and west coordinating response.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang fixed the plan as follows: the three garrisons of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi had 178,800-odd troops; each of the three regional commanders would drill 10,000, the supreme commander 30,000, with 20,000 stationed at Huailai and 10,000 at Yanghe to coordinate east and west.

sentences.zh: 余授鎮監、巡撫以下分練。

translations.literal: The remainder was assigned to garrison commissioners, grand coordinators, and below for divided drilling.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder was assigned to the garrison commissioners, grand coordinators, and ranks below for separate drilling.

sentences.zh: 延綏、寧夏、甘肅、固原、臨兆五鎮兵十五萬五千七百有奇，五總兵各練萬，總督練三萬，以二萬駐固原，一萬駐延安，東西策應。

translations.literal: Yan-sui, Ningxia, Gansu, Guyuan, and Lintao five garrisons' troops 155,700 odd; five regional commanders each drill 10,000, supreme commander drills 30,000, with 20,000 stationed at Guyuan, 10,000 at Yan'an, east and west coordinating response.
translations.idiomatic: The five garrisons of Yan-sui, Ningxia, Gansu, Guyuan, and Lintao had 155,700-odd troops; each of the five regional commanders would drill 10,000, the supreme commander 30,000, with 20,000 at Guyuan and 10,000 at Yan'an to coordinate east and west.

sentences.zh: 余授巡撫、副將以下分練。

translations.literal: The remainder was assigned to grand coordinators, vice commanders, and below for divided drilling.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder was assigned to the grand coordinators, vice commanders, and ranks below for separate drilling.

sentences.zh: 遼東、薊鎮兵二十四萬有奇，五總兵各練萬，總督練五萬，外自錦州，內抵居庸，東西策應。

translations.literal: Liaodong and Jizhou garrisons' troops 240,000 odd; five regional commanders each drill 10,000, supreme commander drills 50,000, outward from Jinzhou, inward reaching Juyong, east and west coordinating response.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong and Jizhou garrisons had 240,000-odd troops; each of the five regional commanders would drill 10,000, the supreme commander 50,000, from Jinzhou on the outside to Juyong on the inside, coordinating east and west.

sentences.zh: 余授鎮監、巡撫以下分練。

translations.literal: The remainder was assigned to garrison commissioners, grand coordinators, and below for divided drilling.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder was assigned to the garrison commissioners, grand coordinators, and ranks below for separate drilling.

sentences.zh: 汰通州、昌平督治二侍郎，設保定一總督，合畿輔、山東、河北兵，得十五萬七千有奇，四總兵各練二萬，總督練三萬，北自昌平，南抵河北，聞警策應。

translations.literal: Eliminate the two vice ministers supervising Tongzhou and Changping, establish one supreme commander at Baoding, combine capital region, Shandong, and Hebei troops, obtaining 157,000 odd; four regional commanders each drill 20,000, supreme commander drills 30,000, north from Changping, south reaching Hebei, responding to alarms.
translations.idiomatic: The two vice ministers supervising Tongzhou and Changping were eliminated, a single supreme commander was established at Baoding, and the troops of the capital region, Shandong, and Hebei were combined into 157,000-odd men; each of the four regional commanders would drill 20,000, the supreme commander 30,000, from Changping in the north to Hebei in the south, ready to respond at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 余授巡撫以下分練。

translations.literal: The remainder was assigned to grand coordinators and below for divided drilling.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder was assigned to the grand coordinators and ranks below for separate drilling.

sentences.zh: 又以畿輔重地，議增監司四人。

translations.literal: Also because the capital region was a vital area, he proposed adding four surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Because the capital region was vital territory, he also proposed adding four surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 於是大名、廣平、順德增一人，真定、保定、河間各一人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Daming, Guangping, and Shunde each gained one; Zhending, Baoding, and Hejian each one.
translations.idiomatic: Daming, Guangping, and Shunde each gained one commissioner; Zhending, Baoding, and Hejian each gained one as well.

sentences.zh: 薊遼總督下增監軍三人。

translations.literal: Under the Jizhou-Liaodong supreme commander three army supervisors were added.
translations.idiomatic: Three army supervisors were added under the Jizhou-Liaodong supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 議上，帝悉從之。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor followed it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor approved it in full.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌所議兵凡七十三萬有奇，然民流餉絀，未嘗有實也。

translations.literal: The troops Sichang proposed totaled 730,000 odd, yet the people drifted away and supplies were short—there never was reality in it.
translations.idiomatic: The troops Sichang proposed totaled more than 730,000, yet with the people displaced and supplies short, the numbers never matched reality.

sentences.zh: 帝又采副將楊德政議，府汰通判，設練備，秩次守備，州汰判官，縣汰主簿，設練總，秩次把總，並受轄於正官，專練民兵。

translations.literal: The emperor also adopted vice commander Yang Dezheng's proposal: prefectures eliminate sub-prefect, establish drill-inspector rank next below garrison commander; prefectures eliminate judge, counties eliminate registrar, establish drill-captain rank next below platoon commander—all under jurisdiction of regular officials, specializing in drilling militia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also adopted the proposal of the vice commander Yang Dezheng: prefectures would eliminate the sub-prefect and establish a drill-inspector rank just below garrison commander; prefectures would eliminate the judge and counties the registrar, establishing a drill-captain rank just below platoon commander—all under the regular officials and devoted solely to drilling militia.

sentences.zh: 府千，州七百，縣五百，捍鄉土，不他調。

translations.literal: Prefectures 1,000, prefectures 700, counties 500, defending native soil, not transferred elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture would field 1,000 men, each sub-prefecture 700, each county 500, to defend their own districts without transfer elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌以勢有緩急，請先行畿輔、山東、河南、山西，從之。

translations.literal: Sichang, because circumstances had urgency and ease, requested first implementing in the capital region, Shandong, Henan, and Shanxi; it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang, judging that circumstances varied in urgency, asked that the plan be implemented first in the capital region, Shandong, Henan, and Shanxi; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 於是有練餉之議。

translations.literal: Thereupon arose deliberation on drill-supply funds.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon arose the proposal for drill-supply levies.

sentences.zh: 初，嗣昌增剿餉，期一年而止。

translations.literal: Initially Sichang increased suppression-supply funds, with a term of one year only.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichang had first increased the suppression levy, it was to last only one year.

sentences.zh: 後餉盡而賊未平，詔征其半。

translations.literal: Later when funds were exhausted and bandits not pacified, an edict levied half.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the funds were exhausted and the rebels still unrested, an edict ordered collection of half the levy.

sentences.zh: 至是，督餉侍郎張伯鯨請全征。

translations.literal: By this time, the supplies-supervising vice minister Zhang Boyu requested full collection.
translations.idiomatic: By this time the supplies-supervising vice minister Zhang Boyu requested full collection of the levy.

sentences.zh: 帝慮失信，嗣昌曰：「無傷也，加賦出於土田，土田盡歸有力家，百畝增銀三四錢，稍抑兼並耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor worried about breaking faith; Sichang said: "No harm—added levies come from land, land all returns to powerful households; per hundred mu add three or four qian of silver, slightly restraining annexation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried about breaking faith with the people; Sichang said, "It does no harm. The added levy comes from land, and land has all passed into the hands of the powerful; an extra three or four qian of silver per hundred mu will only slightly restrain land annexation."

sentences.zh: 大學士薛國觀、程國祥皆贊之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Xue Guanguan and Cheng Guoxiang all approved.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries Xue Guanguan and Cheng Guoxiang both approved.

sentences.zh: 於是剿餉外復增練餉七百三十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon beyond suppression-supply funds, drill-supply funds of 7,300,000 were again added.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, beyond the suppression levy, a drill levy of 7.3 million taels was added.

sentences.zh: 論者謂：「九邊自有額餉，概予新餉，則舊者安歸？

translations.literal: Critics said: "The nine frontiers already have quota supplies—if all are given new supplies, where do the old go?
translations.idiomatic: Critics said, "The nine frontier garrisons already have allotted funds—if everything is assigned to the new levies, what becomes of the old allotments?

sentences.zh: 邊兵多虛額，今指為實數，餉盡虛糜，而練數仍不足。

translations.literal: Frontier troops mostly have phantom rolls; now treating them as real numbers, supplies all wasted in vain, yet drill numbers still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier rolls are mostly padded with phantom men; treating them as real numbers wastes the funds in vain while the drilled troops still fall short.

sentences.zh: 且兵以分防不能常聚，故有抽練之議，抽練而其余遂不問。

translations.literal: Moreover troops because of divided defense cannot always assemble, hence the proposal for selective drilling—selective drilling and the rest then go unasked.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because troops are scattered on defensive duty they cannot always assemble, hence the proposal for selective drilling—but once the select few are drilled, the rest are ignored.

sentences.zh: 且抽練仍虛文，邊防愈益弱。

translations.literal: Moreover selective drilling remains empty form, frontier defense grows weaker still.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, selective drilling remains a paper exercise, and frontier defense grows weaker still.

sentences.zh: 至州縣民兵益無實，徒糜厚餉。」

translations.literal: As for prefecture and county militia, they increasingly have no reality, vainly wasting thick supplies."
translations.idiomatic: As for prefectural and county militia, they increasingly exist only on paper, wasting heavy funds in vain."

sentences.zh: 以嗣昌主之，事鉅莫敢難也。

translations.literal: Because Sichang championed it, the matter was huge and none dared object.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sichang championed the plan, the matter was too large for anyone to dare object.

sentences.zh: 神宗末增賦五百二十萬，崇禎初再增百四十萬，總名遼餉。

translations.literal: At the end of Shenzong's reign levies were increased 5,200,000; at the beginning of Chongzhen again increased 1,400,000, altogether named Liaodong supplies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Shenzong reign levies were increased by 5.2 million taels; at the beginning of Chongzhen they were increased again by 1.4 million, together called the Liaodong levy.

sentences.zh: 至是，復增剿餉、練餉，額溢之。

translations.literal: By this time, suppression and drill supplies were again added, the quota overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: By this time the suppression and drill levies were added as well, and the total quota overflowed.

sentences.zh: 先後增賦千六百七十萬，民不聊生，益起為盜矣。

translations.literal: Successive increases totaled 16,700,000; the people could not sustain life and increasingly rose as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Successive increases totaled 16.7 million taels; the people could barely survive and increasingly turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 五月，熊文燦所撫賊張獻忠反谷城，羅汝才等九營皆反。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the bandit Zhang Xianzhong whom Xiong Wencan had appeased rebelled at Gucheng; Luo Rucai and nine camps all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the rebel Zhang Xianzhong, whom Xiong Wencan had appeased, rebelled at Gucheng; Luo Rucai and nine other camps rebelled as well.

sentences.zh: 八月，傅宗龍抵京，嗣昌解部務，還內閣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Fu Zonglong reached the capital; Sichang relinquished ministry duties and returned to the inner cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fu Zonglong reached the capital; Sichang relinquished his ministry duties and returned to the inner cabinet.

sentences.zh: 未幾，羅𤠉山敗書聞。

translations.literal: Before long, news arrived of defeat at [Xi] Yingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came news of the defeat at Xi Yingshan.

sentences.zh: 帝大驚，詔逮文燦。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly alarmed and ordered Wencan arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly alarmed and ordered Wencan arrested.

sentences.zh: 特旨命嗣昌督師，賜尚方劍，以便宜誅賞。

translations.literal: By special edict Sichang was ordered to supervise the army, granted the imperial sword, with discretionary power to execute and reward.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict Sichang was ordered to take command of the army, granted the imperial sword, and given discretionary power to execute and reward.

sentences.zh: 九月朔，召見平臺。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, he was summoned to audience at the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month he was summoned to audience at the terrace.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌曰：「君言不宿於家，臣朝受命，夕啟行，軍資甲仗望敕所司遄發。」

translations.literal: Sichang said: "The ruler's words do not lodge overnight at home—a subject receives orders in the morning and departs at evening; military supplies and armor hope Your Majesty will order the relevant offices to dispatch swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: Sichang said, "A ruler's command does not spend the night at home—a subject who receives orders in the morning sets out that evening. I beg Your Majesty to order the relevant offices to dispatch military supplies and arms at once."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，曰：「卿能如此，朕復何憂。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said: "If you can be thus, what worry have I?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said, "If you can act thus, what have I to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 翊日，賜白金百、大紅絺絲四表裏、鬥牛衣一、賞功銀四萬、銀牌千五百、幣帛千。

translations.literal: The next day, granted one hundred taels white silver, four suits of great red silk, one Dipper-Ox robe, 40,000 taels merit-reward silver, 1,500 silver plaques, one thousand bolts silk.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was granted one hundred taels of white silver, four suits of great red silk, one Dipper-Ox robe, 40,000 taels of merit-reward silver, 1,500 silver plaques, and one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌條七事以獻，悉報可。

translations.literal: Sichang listed seven items to present; all were reported approved.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang presented seven proposals; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 四日召見賜宴，手觴三爵，御製贈行詩一章。

translations.literal: On the fourth day summoned to audience and granted banquet, personally offered three cups, imperially composed one farewell poem.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day he was summoned again, granted a banquet, and offered three cups with his own hand; the emperor composed a farewell poem.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌跪誦，拜且泣。

translations.literal: Sichang knelt and recited it, bowed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang knelt to recite it, bowed, and wept.

sentences.zh: 越二日，陛辭，賜膳。

translations.literal: Two days later, audience for farewell, granted provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he took leave at court and was granted provisions for the journey.

sentences.zh: 二十九日抵襄陽，入文燦軍。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day he reached Xiangyang and entered Wencan's army.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day he reached Xiangyang and took over Wencan's army.

sentences.zh: 文燦就逮，嗣昌猶為疏辯雲。

translations.literal: Wencan was arrested; Sichang still memorialized in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Wencan was arrested, Sichang still memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，嗣昌大誓三軍，督理中官劉元斌，湖廣巡撫方孔炤，總兵官左良玉、陳洪範等畢會。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, Sichang swore a great oath before the three armies; supervising eunuch Liu Yuanbin, Huguang grand coordinator Fang Kongzhao, regional commanders Zuo Liangyu, Chen Hongfan, and others all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month Sichang swore a great oath before the three armies; the supervising eunuch Liu Yuanbin, the Huguang grand coordinator Fang Kongzhao, the regional commanders Zuo Liangyu and Chen Hongfan, and others all assembled.

sentences.zh: 賊賀一龍等掠葉，圍沈丘，焚項城之郛，寇光山。

translations.literal: The bandits He Yilong and others raided Ye, besieged Shenqiu, burned the outer wall of Xiangcheng, and invaded Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels He Yilong and others raided Ye, besieged Shenqiu, burned the outer wall of Xiangcheng, and invaded Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 副將張琮、刁明忠率京軍逾山行九十里，及其巢。

translations.literal: Vice commanders Zhang Cong and Diao Mingzhong led capital troops over mountains marching ninety li and reached their nest.
translations.idiomatic: The vice commanders Zhang Cong and Diao Mingzhong led capital troops ninety li over the mountains and reached the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 先驅射賊，殪絳袍而馳者二人，追奔四十里，斬首千七百五十。

translations.literal: The vanguard shot at bandits, killing two in crimson robes who fled; pursued forty li, beheading 1,750.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard shot at the rebels and killed two crimson-robed riders in flight; pursuing forty li, they took 1,750 heads.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌稱詔頒賜。

translations.literal: Sichang proclaimed edict to distribute rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang proclaimed an edict distributing rewards.

sentences.zh: 十一月，興世王王國寧以眾千人來歸，受之於襄陽，處其妻子樊城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Prince of the Prosperous Age Wang Guoning came to surrender with a thousand-odd followers; received at Xiangyang, his wife and children placed at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Prince of the Prosperous Age Wang Guoning surrendered with more than a thousand followers; he was received at Xiangyang and his family was settled at Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 表良玉平賊將軍。

translations.literal: He memorialized Liangyu as Pacifying-Bandits General.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Liangyu be titled Pacifying-Rebels General.

sentences.zh: 諸將積驕玩，無鬥誌。

translations.literal: The generals had long been arrogant and negligent, without fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The generals had grown arrogant and negligent, without fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 獻忠、羅汝才、惠登相等八營遁鄖陽、興安山間，掠南漳、谷城、房、竹山、竹溪。

translations.literal: Xianzhong, Luo Rucai, Hui Dengxiang, and eight camps fled into the mountains between Yunyang and Xing'an, raiding Nanzhang, Gucheng, Fang, Zhushan, and Zhuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong, Luo Rucai, Hui Dengxiang, and eight camps fled into the mountains between Yunyang and Xing'an, raiding Nanzhang, Gucheng, Fang, Zhushan, and Zhuxi.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌鞭刁明忠，斬監軍僉事殷大白以徇。

translations.literal: Sichang flogged Diao Mingzhong and executed army-supervising associate commissioner Yin Dabai as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang flogged Diao Mingzhong and executed the army-supervising associate commissioner Yin Dabai as a warning.

sentences.zh: 檄巡撫方孔炤遣楊世恩、羅萬邦剿汝才、登相，全軍覆於香油坪。

translations.literal: He ordered grand coordinator Fang Kongzhao to send Yang Shi'en and Luo Wanbang to suppress Rucai and Dengxiang; the whole army was destroyed at Xiangyouping.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the grand coordinator Fang Kongzhao to send Yang Shi'en and Luo Wanbang against Rucai and Dengxiang; the entire force was destroyed at Xiangyouping.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌劾逮孔炤，奏辟永州推官萬元吉為軍前監紀，從之。

translations.literal: Sichang impeached and arrested Kongzhao, memorialized to appoint Yongzhou magistrate Wan Yuanji as army-front disciplinarian; it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang impeached Kongzhao and had him arrested; he memorialized to appoint the Yongzhou magistrate Wan Yuanji as army-front disciplinarian, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 當是時，李自成潛伏陜右，賀一龍、左金王等四營跳梁漢東，嗣昌專剿獻忠。

translations.literal: At this time Li Zicheng lay hidden in western Shaanxi; He Yilong, Zuo Jinwang, and four camps rampaged in eastern Han; Sichang focused on suppressing Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Zicheng lay hidden in western Shaanxi; He Yilong, Zuo Jinwang, and four camps rampaged in eastern Han; Sichang focused solely on suppressing Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 獻忠屢敗於興安，求撫，不許。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was repeatedly defeated at Xing'an, sought appeasement, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong was repeatedly defeated at Xing'an and sought appeasement, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 其黨托天王常國安、金翅鵬劉希原來降，獻忠走入川，良玉追之。

translations.literal: His followers Trust-in-Heaven King Chang Guo'an and Golden-Wing Peng Liu Xiyuan came to surrender; Xianzhong fled into Sichuan and Liangyu pursued.
translations.idiomatic: His followers Trust-in-Heaven King Chang Guo'an and Golden-Wing Peng Liu Xiyuan surrendered; Xianzhong fled into Sichuan and Liangyu pursued him.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌牒令還，良玉不從。

translations.literal: Sichang sent orders to return; Liangyu did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang sent orders to return; Liangyu disobeyed.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月七日，與陜西副將賀人龍、李國奇夾擊獻忠於瑪瑙山，大破之，斬馘三千六百二十，墜巖谷死者無算。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the second month of the thirteenth year, together with Shaanxi vice commanders He Renlong and Li Guoqi, he attacked Xianzhong from both sides at Agate Mountain, routing him greatly; beheaded and captured 3,620; those who fell into cliffs and ravines and died were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the second month of the thirteenth year, together with the Shaanxi vice commanders He Renlong and Li Guoqi, he attacked Xianzhong from both sides at Agate Mountain and routed him utterly, taking 3,620 heads; those who fell into cliffs and ravines and died were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 其黨掃地王曹威等授首，十反王楊友賢率眾降。

translations.literal: His followers Sweeping-Earth King Cao Wei and others presented their heads; Ten-Rebellions King Yang Youxian led the masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His followers Sweeping-Earth King Cao Wei and others surrendered their heads; Ten-Rebellions King Yang Youxian led his band to surrender.

sentences.zh: 是月也，帝念嗣昌，發銀萬兩犒師，賜鬥牛衣、良馬、金鞍各二。

translations.literal: That month the emperor thought of Sichang, issued 10,000 taels silver to reward the army, granted two Dipper-Ox robes, fine horses, and gold saddles each.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor thought of Sichang, sent 10,000 taels of silver to reward the army, and granted him two Dipper-Ox robes, fine horses, and gold saddles.

sentences.zh: 使者甫出國門，而瑪瑙山之捷至，大悅，再發銀五萬，幣帛千犒師。

translations.literal: The envoy had just left the capital gate when news of victory at Agate Mountain arrived; greatly pleased, again issued 50,000 taels silver and one thousand bolts silk to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy had just left the capital when news of the victory at Agate Mountain arrived; greatly pleased, the emperor sent another 50,000 taels of silver and one thousand bolts of silk to reward the army.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was given additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 而湖廣將張應元、汪之鳳敗賊水右壩，獲其軍師。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Huguang generals Zhang Yingyuan and Wang Zhifeng defeated bandits at Shuiyouba and captured their military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Huguang generals Zhang Yingyuan and Wang Zhifeng defeated the rebels at Shuiyouba and captured their military adviser.

sentences.zh: 四川將張令、方國安敗之千江河。

translations.literal: Sichuan generals Zhang Ling and Fang Guo'an defeated them at Qianjiang River.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan generals Zhang Ling and Fang Guo'an defeated them at Qianjiang River.

sentences.zh: 李國奇、賀人龍等敗之寒溪寺、鹽井。

translations.literal: Li Guoqi, He Renlong, and others defeated them at Hanxi Temple and Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guoqi, He Renlong, and others defeated them at Hanxi Temple and Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 川、陜、湖廣諸將畢集，復連敗之黃墩、木瓜溪，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Huguang generals all assembled and again repeatedly defeated them at Huangdun and Mugua Stream; military renown greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: The generals of Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Huguang all assembled and again defeated them in succession at Huangdun and Mugua Stream; military morale revived greatly.

sentences.zh: 汝才、登相求撫，獻忠持之，斂兵南漳、遠安間，殺安撫官姚宗中，走大寧、大昌，犯巫山，為川中患。

translations.literal: Rucai and Dengxiang sought appeasement; Xianzhong held them back, gathered troops between Nanzhang and Yuan'an, killed pacification official Yao Zongzhong, fled to Daning and Dachang, invaded Wushan, becoming a scourge in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai and Dengxiang sought appeasement, but Xianzhong held them back; he gathered his forces between Nanzhang and Yuan'an, killed the pacification official Yao Zongzhong, fled to Daning and Dachang, invaded Wushan, and became a scourge in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 獻忠遁興安、平利山中，良玉圍而不攻，賊得收散亡，由興安、房縣走白羊山而西，與汝才等合。

translations.literal: Xianzhong fled into the mountains of Xing'an and Pingli; Liangyu besieged but did not attack; the bandits were able to gather scattered fugitives, from Xing'an and Fang counties fled west by Baiyang Mountain, and united with Rucai and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong fled into the mountains of Xing'an and Pingli; Liangyu besieged but did not attack, allowing the rebels to regather their scattered forces; they fled west from Xing'an and Fang counties by way of Baiyang Mountain and united with Rucai and others.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌以群賊合，其勢復張，乃由襄陽赴夷陵，扼其要害。

translations.literal: Sichang, because the bandit groups united and their power revived, then went from Xiangyang to Yiling to choke their vital point.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the rebel bands unite and their power revive, Sichang went from Xiangyang to Yiling to block their vital line of advance.

sentences.zh: 帝念嗣昌行間勞苦，賜敕發賞功銀萬，賜鞍馬二。

translations.literal: The emperor thought of Sichang's hardships in the field, granted edict to issue 10,000 taels merit-reward silver, granted two saddled horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful of Sichang's hardships in the field, granted an edict issuing 10,000 taels of merit-reward silver and two saddled horses.

sentences.zh: 罷鄖陽撫治王鰲永，詔廢將猛如虎軍前立功。

translations.literal: Dismissed Yunyang pacification commissioner Wang Aoyong; edict ordered dismissed general Meng Ruhu to achieve merit before the army.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed the Yunyang pacification commissioner Wang Aoyong and ordered the dismissed general Meng Ruhu to win merit at the front.

sentences.zh: 黃得功、宋紀大破賊商城，賀一龍五大部降而復叛。

translations.literal: Huang Degong and Song Ji greatly defeated bandits at Shangcheng; He Yilong's five great divisions surrendered then rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Degong and Song Ji inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Shangcheng; He Yilong's five major divisions surrendered and then rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 鄭嘉棟、賀人龍大破汝才、登相開縣。

translations.literal: Zheng Jiadong and He Renlong greatly defeated Rucai and Dengxiang at Kaixian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jiadong and He Renlong inflicted a great defeat on Rucai and Dengxiang at Kaixian.

sentences.zh: 汝才偕小秦王東奔，登相越開縣而西，自是二賊始分。

translations.literal: Rucai together with Little Qin King fled east; Dengxiang crossed Kaixian and went west — from this the two bandits first split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai fled east together with Little Qin King, while Dengxiang crossed Kaixian and headed west; from that point the two rebel bands parted ways.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸部士馬居山谷，罹炎暑瘴毒，物故十二三。

translations.literal: At this time troops and horses of the various units dwelt in mountain valleys, suffered heat, summer fever, and miasmic poison; one or two in ten perished.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the troops and horses of the various units were encamped in mountain valleys, where they suffered heat, summer fevers, and malarial miasma; one or two soldiers in ten died.

sentences.zh: 京兵之在荊門、雲南兵之在簡坪、湖廣兵之在馬蝗坡者，久屯思歸，夜亡多。

translations.literal: Capital troops at Jingmen, Yunnan troops at Jianping, Huguang troops at Mahuangpo — having encamped long they longed to return; many fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The capital troops at Jingmen, the Yunnan troops at Jianping, and the Huguang troops at Mahuang Slope had been encamped so long that they yearned to go home, and many deserted by night.

sentences.zh: 關河大旱，人相食，土寇蜂起，陜西竇開遠、河南李際遇為之魁，饑民從之，所在告警。

translations.literal: In the Guanne and Hexi regions great drought; people ate one another; local bandits swarmed; Shaanxi's Dou Kaiyuan and Henan's Li Jiyu were their chiefs; starving people followed them; alarm was raised everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Severe drought struck the Guanne and Hexi regions, people resorted to cannibalism, and local bandits rose everywhere; Dou Kaiyuan of Shaanxi and Li Jiyu of Henan became their leaders, starving peasants joined them, and alarms were raised in every quarter.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌以聞。

translations.literal: Sichang reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang reported these developments to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝發帑金五萬，營醫藥，責諸將進兵。

translations.literal: The emperor issued 50,000 taels from the treasury, organized medical supplies, and ordered the generals to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released 50,000 taels from the treasury, arranged for medical supplies, and ordered the generals to advance.

sentences.zh: 而陜之長武，川之新寧、大竹，湖廣之羅田又相繼報陷。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Changwu in Shaanxi, Xinning and Dazhu in Sichuan, and Luotian in Huguang in succession reported fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Reports then came in succession that Changwu in Shaanxi, Xinning and Dazhu in Sichuan, and Luotian in Huguang had all fallen.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌乃下招撫令，為諭帖萬紙，散之賊中。

translations.literal: Sichang then issued appeasement orders, made ten thousand proclamation sheets, and scattered them among the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang then issued orders of appeasement, had ten thousand proclamation sheets printed, and distributed them among the rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 七月，監軍孔貞會等大破汝才豐邑坪。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, supervising generals Kong Zhenhui and others greatly defeated Rucai at Fengyiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the supervising generals Kong Zhenhui and others inflicted a great defeat on Rucai at Fengyiping.

sentences.zh: 其黨混世王、小秦王率其下降，賊魁整十萬及登相、王光恩亦相繼降，於是群賊盡萃於蜀中。

translations.literal: His followers Chaos King and Little Qin King led their bands to surrender; bandit chieftain Zheng Shawan, Dengxiang, and Wang Guang'en also surrendered in succession; thus all bandits gathered in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His followers Chaos King and Little Qin King led their bands in surrender; the rebel chieftain Zheng Shawan, along with Dengxiang and Wang Guang'en, also surrendered in turn, and all the rebel bands then gathered in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌遂入川，以八月泛舟上，謂川地厄塞，諸軍合而蹙之，可盡殄。

translations.literal: Sichang then entered Sichuan; in the eighth month he went upstream by boat, saying Sichuan terrain was narrow and blocked — if all armies united and pressed them, they could be utterly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang then entered Sichuan and, in the eighth month, went upstream by boat, reasoning that Sichuan's terrain was narrow and defensible and that if all the armies united to press the rebels, they could be wiped out entirely.

sentences.zh: 而人龍以秦師自開縣噪而西歸，應元等敗績於夔之土地嶺，獻忠勢復張，汝才與之合。

translations.literal: But Renlong led Qin troops in mutiny from Kaixian and marched west homeward; Yingyuan and others were defeated at Tudiling in Kui; Xianzhong's power revived again; Rucai joined him.
translations.idiomatic: But Renlong led his Qin troops in mutiny from Kaixian and marched west toward home; Yingyuan and others were defeated at Tudiling in Kui; Xianzhong's strength revived, and Rucai rejoined him.

sentences.zh: 聞督師西，遂急趨大昌，犯觀音巖，守將邵仲光不能禦，遂突凈壁，陷大昌。

translations.literal: Hearing the supreme commander had gone west, they hurried to Dachang, attacked Guanyin Cliff; defending general Shao Zhongguang could not hold them; they broke through Jingbi and took Dachang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the supreme commander had gone west, they rushed toward Dachang, attacked Guanyin Cliff, and when the defending general Shao Zhongguang could not hold them, broke through Jingbi and captured Dachang.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌斬仲光，劾逮四川巡撫邵捷春。

translations.literal: Sichang executed Zhongguang and impeached and arrested Sichuan grand coordinator Shao Jiechun.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang executed Zhongguang and impeached the Sichuan grand coordinator Shao Jiechun, who was arrested.

sentences.zh: 賊遂渡河至通江，嗣昌至萬縣。

translations.literal: The bandits then crossed the river to Tongjiang; Sichang reached Wanxian.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then crossed the river to Tongjiang, while Sichang reached Wanxian.

sentences.zh: 賊攻巴州不下，嗣昌至梁山，檄諸將分擊。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked Bazhou but did not take it; Sichang reached Liangshan and ordered the generals to strike separately.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked Bazhou but failed to take it; Sichang reached Liangshan and ordered the generals to attack on separate fronts.

sentences.zh: 賊已陷劍州，趨保寧，將由間道入漢中。

translations.literal: The bandits had already taken Jianzhou, marched toward Baoning, and were about to enter Hanzhong by a bypath.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already captured Jianzhou and were advancing on Baoning, intending to enter Hanzhong by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 趙光遠、賀人龍拒之，賊乃轉掠，陷梓潼、昭化，抵綿州，將趨成都。

translations.literal: Zhao Guangyuan and He Renlong blocked them; the bandits then turned to plunder, took Zitong and Zhaohua, reached Mianzhou, and were about to march on Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guangyuan and He Renlong blocked them, so the rebels turned to raiding instead, captured Zitong and Zhaohua, reached Mianzhou, and were about to march on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，嗣昌至重慶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Sichang reached Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Sichang arrived at Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 賊攻羅江，不克，走綿竹。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked Luojiang but did not take it and fled to Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked Luojiang but failed to capture it and withdrew toward Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌至順慶，諸將不會師。

translations.literal: Sichang reached Shunqing; the generals did not unite for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang reached Shunqing, but the generals failed to assemble for a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 賊轉掠至漢州，去中江百里，守將方國安避之去，賊遂縱掠什邡、綿竹、安縣、德陽、金堂間，所至空城而遁，全蜀大震。
