translations.literal: The bandits turned to plunder and reached Hanzhou, a hundred li from Zhongjiang; defending general Fang Guo'an avoided them and left; the bandits then freely plundered between Shifang, Mianzhu, Anxian, Deyang, and Jintang; wherever they went cities were emptied and they fled; all Sichuan was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned to raiding and reached Hanzhou, a hundred li from Zhongjiang; the defending general Fang Guo'an fled before them, and they then rampaged through Shifang, Mianzhu, Anxian, Deyang, and Jintang, leaving every city they touched empty before moving on; all of Sichuan was shaken.

sentences.zh: 賊遂由水道下簡州、資陽。

translations.literal: The bandits then went down by water route to Jianzhou and Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then descended by water to Jianzhou and Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌征諸將合擊，皆退縮。

translations.literal: Sichang summoned the generals for a joint attack; all shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang summoned the generals for a combined assault, but all of them held back.

sentences.zh: 屢征良玉兵，又不至。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he summoned Liangyu's troops, but they did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly summoned Liangyu's troops, but they never arrived.

sentences.zh: 賊遂陷榮昌、永川。

translations.literal: The bandits then took Rongchang and Yongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then captured Rongchang and Yongchuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，陷瀘州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they took Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they captured Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 自賊再入川，諸將無一邀擊者。

translations.literal: Since the bandits re-entered Sichuan, not one general had intercepted them.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the rebels re-entered Sichuan, not a single general had intercepted them.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌雖屢檄，令不行。

translations.literal: Though Sichang repeatedly issued orders, his commands were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Though Sichang issued order after order, his commands went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 其在重慶也，下令赦汝才罪，降則授官，惟獻忠不赦，擒斬者賚萬金，爵侯。

translations.literal: While at Chongqing, he ordered pardon for Rucai's crimes — surrender would bring office; only Xianzhong was not pardoned; whoever captured and killed him would receive 10,000 taels of gold and a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: While at Chongqing he issued an order pardoning Rucai's crimes and offering office to those who surrendered; only Xianzhong was excluded from pardon, with a reward of ten thousand taels of gold and a marquisate for whoever captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，自堂皇至庖湢，遍題「有斬督師獻者，賚白金三錢」，嗣昌駭愕，疑左右皆賊，勒三日進兵。

translations.literal: The next day, from the main hall to the kitchens, everywhere was inscribed: "Whoever presents the head of the supreme commander will receive three qian of white silver"; Sichang was shocked and alarmed, suspected those around him were all bandits, and ordered troops to advance within three days.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, from the main hall to the kitchens, everywhere was scrawled: "Whoever brings in the supreme commander's head will receive three qian of silver"; Sichang was horrified, suspected that those around him were all rebel agents, and ordered the army to advance within three days.

sentences.zh: 會雨雪道斷，復戒期。

translations.literal: But snow and rain blocked the roads, and the deadline was postponed again.
translations.idiomatic: Snow and rain then cut the roads, and the deadline was postponed once more.

sentences.zh: 三檄人龍，不奉令。

translations.literal: Three times he summoned Renlong; he did not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he summoned Renlong, but Renlong refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 初，嗣昌表良玉平賊將軍，良玉浸驕，欲貴人龍以抗之。

translations.literal: Initially Sichang had memorialized to appoint Liangyu Pacification General; Liangyu grew increasingly arrogant and wanted to elevate Renlong to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sichang had memorialized to appoint Liangyu Pacification General; Liangyu grew increasingly arrogant and sought to elevate Renlong as a counterweight.

sentences.zh: 既以瑪瑙山功不果，人龍慍，反以情告良玉，良玉亦慍，語載良玉、人龍傳。

translations.literal: When the Agate Mountain merit failed to materialize, Renlong grew resentful and in turn told Liangyu his grievance; Liangyu too grew resentful — the account is in the biographies of Liangyu and Renlong.
translations.idiomatic: When the promised reward for Agate Mountain failed to materialize, Renlong grew resentful and confided his grievance to Liangyu, who was also angered; the full account is given in the biographies of Liangyu and Renlong.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌雖有才，然好自用，躬親簿書，過於繁碎。

translations.literal: Sichang though talented, yet loved to act on his own; he personally handled ledgers and documents, overly minute and tedious.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang was capable, but he insisted on doing everything himself, personally handling ledgers and paperwork in excessive detail.

sentences.zh: 軍行必自裁進止，千里待報，坐失機會。

translations.literal: On campaign he always decided advance and halt himself; a thousand li awaited his report; opportunities were lost by sitting idle.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he always decided for himself when to advance or halt; armies a thousand li away waited for his word, and opportunities were lost while they sat idle.

sentences.zh: 王鰲永嘗諫之，不納。

translations.literal: Wang Aoyong once remonstrated with him; he did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Aoyong once remonstrated with him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及鰲永罷官，上書於朝曰：「嗣昌用師一年，蕩平未奏，此非謀慮之不長，正由操心之太苦也。

translations.literal: After Aoyong was dismissed from office, he submitted a memorial to the court saying: "Sichang has used troops for a year without reporting pacification — this is not because his planning is poor, but precisely because his labor of mind is too exhausting.
translations.idiomatic: After Aoyong was dismissed, he submitted a memorial to the court saying: "Sichang has commanded troops for a year without achieving pacification — this is not because his plans are unsound, but because he overtaxes himself with minutiae.

sentences.zh: 天下事，總挈大綱則易，獨周萬目則難。

translations.literal: Affairs under heaven, if one grasps the general outline are easy; if one examines every detail alone are difficult.
translations.idiomatic: In affairs under heaven, grasping the broad outline is easy; trying to scrutinize every detail by oneself is hard.

sentences.zh: 況賊情瞬息更變，今舉數千里征伐機宜，盡出嗣昌一人，文牒往返，動逾旬月，坐失事機，無怪乎經年之不戰也。

translations.literal: Moreover bandit conditions change in an instant; now the strategies for campaigns over several thousand li all come from Sichang alone; documents go back and forth, often taking more than ten days and a month; opportunities are lost sitting idle — no wonder there is no battle for a year.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover rebel movements shift in an instant; yet now the plans for campaigns stretching thousands of li all issue from Sichang alone, with dispatches going back and forth often taking more than ten days or a month — opportunities are lost while armies wait, and it is no wonder there has been no fighting for a year.

sentences.zh: 其間能自出奇者，惟瑪瑙山一役。

translations.literal: Among these the one who could produce surprise victory on his own was only the Agate Mountain engagement.
translations.idiomatic: In all this time, the only occasion when a commander could act on his own initiative and win a surprise victory was the battle at Agate Mountain.

sentences.zh: 若必遵督輔號令，良玉當退守興安，無此捷矣。

translations.literal: If he had had to obey the supreme commander's orders, Liangyu would have retreated to hold Xing'an — there would not have been this victory.
translations.idiomatic: If Liangyu had been required to obey the supreme commander's orders, he would have fallen back to hold Xing'an, and that victory would never have happened.

sentences.zh: 臣以為陛下之任嗣昌，不必令其與諸將同功罪，但責其提衡諸將之功罪。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that in the emperor's employing Sichang, it is not necessary to make him share merit and blame equally with the generals, but only to hold him responsible for weighing the merit and blame of the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that in employing Sichang, Your Majesty need not hold him to the same standard of merit and blame as the field generals, but need only charge him with weighing their merits and faults.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌之馭諸將，不必人人授以機宜，但核其機宜之當否，則嗣昌心有余閑，自能決奇制勝。

translations.literal: In Sichang's controlling the generals, it is not necessary to give each man battle plans, but only to examine whether their plans are sound — then Sichang would have surplus mind and leisure, and naturally could decide surprise victories.
translations.idiomatic: In controlling his generals, Sichang need not draw up battle plans for each man himself, but need only judge whether their plans are sound; then he would have mind to spare and could devise the decisive strokes that win battles.

sentences.zh: 何至久延歲月，老師糜餉為哉？」

translations.literal: Why must months drag on, the army grow old, and provisions be wasted?
translations.idiomatic: Why should months drag on, armies sit idle, and provisions be squandered?"

sentences.zh: 先是，嗣昌以諸將進止不一，納幕下評事元吉言，用猛如虎為總統，張應元副之。

translations.literal: First, because the generals' advance and halt were not uniform, Sichang adopted the advice of his staff adviser Yuanji and appointed Meng Ruhu as overall commander with Zhang Yingyuan as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because the generals' movements were uncoordinated, Sichang took the advice of his staff adviser Yuanji and appointed Meng Ruhu overall commander, with Zhang Yingyuan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 比賊入瀘州，如虎及賀人龍、趙光遠軍至，賊復渡南溪，越成都，走漢州、德陽、綿州、劍州、昭化至廣元，又走巴州、達州。

translations.literal: By the time the bandits entered Luzhou, Ruhu and He Renlong and Zhao Guangyuan's armies arrived; the bandits again crossed Nanxi, passed Chengdu, fled through Hanzhou, Deyang, Mianzhou, Jianzhou, Zhaohua to Guangyuan, then fled to Bazhou and Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the rebels entered Luzhou, the armies of Ruhu, He Renlong, and Zhao Guangyuan had arrived; the rebels again crossed the Nanxi River, passed Chengdu, and fled through Hanzhou, Deyang, Mianzhou, Jianzhou, and Zhaohua to Guangyuan, then on to Bazhou and Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 諸軍疲極，惟如虎軍躡其後。

translations.literal: The armies were utterly exhausted; only Ruhu's army trailed behind them.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were utterly exhausted; only Ruhu's force still pressed on their heels.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，嗣昌知賊必出川，遂統舟師下雲陽，檄諸軍陸行追賊。

translations.literal: First month of the fourteenth year — Sichang knew the bandits must leave Sichuan, so he led the fleet downstream to Yunyang and ordered the armies to pursue by land.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year, Sichang knew the rebels would have to leave Sichuan, so he led the fleet downstream to Yunyang and ordered the land forces to pursue them.

sentences.zh: 人龍軍既噪而西，頓兵廣元不進，所恃惟如虎。

translations.literal: Renlong's army had already mutinied westward; they halted troops at Guangyuan and did not advance; what he relied on was only Ruhu.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong's army had already mutinied and marched west; his troops halted at Guangyuan and would not advance, and Sichang's only reliance was Ruhu.

sentences.zh: 比與賊戰開縣、黃陵城，大敗，將士死亡過半。

translations.literal: When they fought the bandits at Kaixian and Huanglingcheng, they were greatly defeated; more than half the officers and soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: When they fought the rebels at Kaixian and Huanglingcheng, they suffered a crushing defeat, and more than half the officers and soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 如虎突圍免，馬騾關防盡為賊有。

translations.literal: Ruhu broke out of encirclement and escaped; horses, mules, and tally-passports were all taken by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhu broke out of the encirclement and escaped, but the horses, mules, and military tallies all fell into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 初，賊竄南溪，元吉欲從間道出梓潼，扼歸路以待賊。

translations.literal: Initially when the bandits fled to Nanxi, Yuanji wanted to take a bypath out to Zitong and block the return route to wait for the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first fled toward Nanxi, Yuanji wanted to take a hidden route through Zitong and block their line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌檄諸軍躡賊疾追，不得拒賊遠，令他逸。

translations.literal: Sichang ordered all armies to press close in swift pursuit and not block the bandits from afar, letting them escape.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang ordered all the armies to press close in swift pursuit and not try to block the rebels from a distance, lest they slip away.

sentences.zh: 諸將乃盡從瀘州逐後塵。

translations.literal: The generals then all followed from Luzhou chasing their rear.
translations.idiomatic: The generals then all set out from Luzhou in pursuit, chasing only the rebels' rear.

sentences.zh: 賊折而東返，歸路盡空，不可復遏，嗣昌始悔不用元吉言。

translations.literal: The bandits turned east and returned; the return route was entirely empty; they could no longer be stopped; Sichang then regretted not taking Yuanji's advice.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned east and headed back, finding the return route entirely undefended; they could no longer be stopped, and Sichang then regretted not heeding Yuanji's advice.

sentences.zh: 賊遂下夔門，抵興山，攻當陽，犯荊門。

translations.literal: The bandits then went down through Kuimen, reached Xingshan, attacked Dangyang, and invaded Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then descended through Kuimen, reached Xingshan, attacked Dangyang, and invaded Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌至夷陵，檄良玉兵，使十九返。

translations.literal: Sichang reached Yiling and summoned Liangyu's troops — nineteen times he sent summons.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang reached Yiling and summoned Liangyu's troops, sending messengers nineteen times.

sentences.zh: 良玉撤興、房兵趨漢中，若相避然。

translations.literal: Liangyu withdrew Xing and Fang troops toward Hanzhong, as if deliberately avoiding them.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu withdrew his Xing and Fang troops toward Hanzhong, as though deliberately avoiding the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊所至，燒驛舍，殺塘卒，東西消息中斷。

translations.literal: Wherever the bandits went they burned relay stations, killed courier-station soldiers; east-west communications were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the rebels went they burned relay stations and killed courier-station guards, cutting off communications east and west.

sentences.zh: 鄖陽撫治袁繼鹹聞賊至當陽，急謀發兵。

translations.literal: Yunyang pacification commissioner Yuan Jixian heard the bandits had reached Dangyang and urgently planned to dispatch troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunyang pacification commissioner Yuan Jixian heard that the rebels had reached Dangyang and urgently set about raising troops.

sentences.zh: 獻忠令汝才與相持，而自以輕騎一日夜馳三百里，殺督師使者於道，取軍符。

translations.literal: Xianzhong ordered Rucai to hold them in check while he himself with light cavalry in one day and one night raced three hundred li, killed the supreme commander's messenger on the road, and seized the military tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong ordered Rucai to hold the government forces in check while he himself, with light cavalry, rode three hundred li in a single day and night, killed the supreme commander's messenger on the road, and seized the military tallies.

sentences.zh: 以二月十一日抵襄陽近郊，用二十八騎持軍符先馳呼城門督師調兵，守者合符而信，入之。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the second month he reached the outskirts of Xiangyang; twenty-eight horsemen holding the military tallies rode ahead calling at the gate that the supreme commander was transferring troops; the defenders matched the tallies and believed, and let them in.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the second month he reached the outskirts of Xiangyang; twenty-eight horsemen bearing the military tallies rode ahead to the gate, calling out that the supreme commander was redeploying troops; the guards matched the tallies, believed them, and let them in.

sentences.zh: 夜半從中起，城遂陷。

translations.literal: At midnight they rose from within; the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they rose from within the city, and Xiangyang fell.

sentences.zh: 獻忠縛襄王置堂下，屬之酒，曰：「吾欲斷楊嗣昌頭，嗣昌在遠。

translations.literal: Xianzhong bound the Prince of Xiang and placed him below the hall, offered him wine, and said: "I wish to cut off Yang Sichang's head, but Sichang is far away.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong bound the Prince of Xiang and placed him below the hall, offered him wine, and said: "I want to cut off Yang Sichang's head, but Sichang is far away.

sentences.zh: 今借王頭，俾嗣昌以陷藩伏法。

translations.literal: Now I borrow your head, so Sichang may be executed for letting a prince fall captive.
translations.idiomatic: Now I will borrow Your Highness's head, so that Sichang may be punished by law for letting a prince fall.

sentences.zh: 王努力盡此酒。」

translations.literal: Prince, exert yourself and drain this cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness, do your best and finish this cup of wine."

sentences.zh: 遂害之。

translations.literal: Then he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: With that he put the prince to death.

sentences.zh: 未幾，渡漢水，走河南，與賀一龍、左金王諸賊合。

translations.literal: Before long, he crossed the Han River, fled to Henan, and united with He Yilong, Zuo Jinwang, and other bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he crossed the Han River, fled into Henan, and joined forces with He Yilong, Zuo Jinwang, and the other rebel bands.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌初以襄陽重鎮，仞深溝方洫而三環之，造飛梁，設橫枑，陳利兵而譏訶，非符要合者不得渡。

translations.literal: Sichang had originally because Xiangyang was a vital stronghold, dug deep moats and square ditches encircling it thrice, built flying bridges, set crossbars, arrayed sharp troops and interrogated — those without matching tallies could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang had originally treated Xiangyang as a vital stronghold, digging deep moats and square ditches in three rings around it, building flying bridges, setting crossbars, and posting sharp troops to challenge passersby — no one without matching tallies could cross.

sentences.zh: 江、漢間列城數十，倚襄陽為天險，賊乃出不意而破之。

translations.literal: Several tens of walled cities between the Yangtze and Han relied on Xiangyang as natural barrier; the bandits yet took it unexpectedly.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen walled cities between the Yangtze and Han relied on Xiangyang as their natural fortress, yet the rebels took it when no one expected it.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌在夷陵，驚悸，上疏請死，下至荊州之沙市，聞洛陽已於正月被陷，福王遇害，益憂懼，遂不食。

translations.literal: Sichang at Yiling was shocked and frightened; submitted memorial asking to die; went down to Shashi in Jingzhou; heard Luoyang had already fallen in the first month and Prince Fu was killed; grew more anxious and fearful; then stopped eating.
translations.idiomatic: At Yiling Sichang was shaken with fear; he submitted a memorial asking to die, then went down to Shashi in Jingzhou; there he learned that Luoyang had fallen in the first month and that Prince Fu had been killed; his anxiety deepened, and he stopped eating.

sentences.zh: 以三月朔日卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month he died, age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month he died at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 廷臣聞襄陽之變，交章論列，而嗣昌已死矣。

translations.literal: Court officials hearing of the Xiangyang disaster submitted memorials criticizing in turn; but Sichang was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials heard of the disaster at Xiangyang, they submitted memorial after memorial assigning blame, but Sichang was already dead.

sentences.zh: 繼鹹及河南巡按高名衡以自裁聞，其子則以病卒報，莫能明也。

translations.literal: Jixian and Henan investigating censor Gao Mingheng were reported to have killed themselves; his son reported he died of illness — none could clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian and the Henan investigating censor Gao Mingheng were reported to have taken their own lives, while Sichang's son reported that he had died of illness — no one could establish the truth.

sentences.zh: 帝甚傷悼之，命丁啟睿代督師。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply grieved; ordered Ding Qirui to replace him as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved and ordered Ding Qirui to replace him as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 傳諭廷臣：「輔臣二載辛勞，一朝畢命，然功不掩過，其議罪以聞。」

translations.literal: Edict transmitted to court officials: "The grand secretary toiled two years and perished in a day — yet merit does not cover fault; discuss guilt and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was transmitted to the court officials: "The grand secretary toiled for two years and perished in a single day; yet merit does not cover fault — discuss his guilt and report back."

sentences.zh: 定國公徐允禎等請以失陷城寨律議斬。

translations.literal: Duke of Dingguo Xu Yunzhen and others asked that under the law for lost cities and forts he be sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Dingguo Xu Yunzhen and others asked that he be sentenced to decapitation under the law governing the loss of cities and forts.

sentences.zh: 上傳制曰：「故輔嗣昌奉命督剿，無城守專責，乃詐城夜襲之檄，嚴飭再三，地方若罔聞知。

translations.literal: The emperor transmitted decree: "The late grand secretary Sichang received orders to supervise suppression — he had no sole charge of defending cities — yet edicts about the night raid with forged tallies were repeatedly sent in strict warning; the local officials seemed not to hear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor transmitted a decree: "The late grand secretary Sichang was ordered to supervise the suppression of rebels and bore no sole responsibility for defending cities; yet edicts warning of the night raid with forged tallies were sent again and again in the strictest terms, and the local officials seemed to hear nothing.

sentences.zh: 及違制陷城，專罪督輔，非通論。

translations.literal: When the city fell in violation of orders, to blame the supreme commander alone is not sound reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: To hold the supreme commander solely responsible when a city falls in violation of orders is not equitable.

sentences.zh: 且臨戎二載，屢著捷功，盡瘁殞身，勤勞難泯。」

translations.literal: Moreover campaigning two years he repeatedly achieved victories; exhausted himself unto death; labor hard to efface.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he campaigned for two years, won repeated victories, exhausted himself unto death, and his devoted service cannot be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 乃昭雪嗣昌罪，賜祭，歸其喪於武陵。

translations.literal: Then cleared Sichang's guilt, granted sacrifice, returned his coffin to Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He then cleared Sichang of guilt, granted him a state sacrifice, and had his coffin returned to Wuling.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌先以剿賊功進太子少傅，既死，論臨、藍平盜功，進太子太傅。

translations.literal: Sichang had earlier for suppression merit been promoted Junior Guardian of Heir Apparent; after death, discussing merit pacifying Lin and Lan bandits, promoted Senior Guardian of Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang had earlier been promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent for his merit in suppressing rebels; after his death, his merit in pacifying the Lin and Lan bandits was recognized with promotion to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 廷臣猶追論不已，帝終念之。

translations.literal: Court officials still pursued criticism without cease; the emperor ultimately remembered him fondly.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials continued to press their criticisms, but the emperor never ceased to think kindly of him.

sentences.zh: 後獻忠陷武陵，心恨嗣昌，發其七世祖墓，焚嗣昌夫婦柩，斷其屍見血，其子孫獲半體改葬焉。

translations.literal: Later when Xianzhong took Wuling, hating Sichang, he dug up his seventh-generation ancestor's tomb, burned the coffins of Sichang and his wife, severed the corpses until blood flowed; descendants recovered half the bodies and reburied them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xianzhong captured Wuling, he bore a grudge against Sichang, dug up the tomb of his seventh-generation ancestor, burned the coffins of Sichang and his wife, and hacked the corpses until blood flowed; Sichang's descendants recovered what remained of the bodies and reburied them.

sentences.zh: 吳甡，字鹿友，揚州興化人。

translations.literal: Wu Shen, styled Luyou, was a native of Xinghua in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen, styled Luyou, was a native of Xinghua in Yangzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知邵武、晉江、濰縣。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Shaowu, Jinjiang, and Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive appointments as magistrate of Shaowu, Jinjiang, and Weixian.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年征授御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tianqi reign he was summoned to office and appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 初入臺，趙南星擬以年例出之，甡乃薦方震孺等，而追論崔文升、李可灼罪，遂得留。

translations.literal: When first entering the Censorate, Zhao Nanxing planned to remove him by seniority rule; Shen then recommended Fang Zhenru and others, and pursued charges against Cui Wensheng and Li Kezhuo; thus he was retained.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the Censorate, Zhao Nanxing planned to remove him under the seniority rule; Shen then recommended Fang Zhenru and others and pursued charges against Cui Wensheng and Li Kezhuo, and so was allowed to remain.

sentences.zh: 後又諫內操宜罷，請召還鄒元標、馮從吾、文震孟，乃積與魏忠賢忤。

translations.literal: Later he also remonstrated that inner-court military drills should cease; requested recall of Zou Yuanbiao, Feng Congwu, and Wen Zhenmeng; thus accumulated conflict with Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also remonstrated that the inner-court military drills should be abolished and requested the recall of Zou Yuanbiao, Feng Congwu, and Wen Zhenmeng, and in this way steadily came into conflict with Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 七年二月削其籍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year his name was struck from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，起故官。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen changed the reign era, he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen reign began, he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁訐錢謙益，周延儒助之。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren impeached Qian Qianyi; Zhou Yanru assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren impeached Qian Qianyi, and Zhou Yanru backed him.

sentences.zh: 甡恐帝即用二人，言枚卜大典當就廷推中簡用，事乃止。

translations.literal: Shen feared the emperor would immediately appoint the two; said the grand selection ceremony should choose from court nomination; the matter then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shen feared the emperor would immediately appoint the two men and argued that the grand appointment ceremony should select from those nominated by the court; the matter then came to a halt.

sentences.zh: 時大治忠賢黨，又值京察，甡言此輩罪惡非考功法所能盡，宜先定其罪，毋混察典。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch faction was being purged; also coincided with capital evaluation; Shen said these men's crimes could not be exhausted by evaluation for merit and demerit — should first fix their guilt, not mix with evaluation statutes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the eunuch faction was being purged, and the capital evaluation was also underway; Shen argued that the crimes of these men could not be fully accounted for under the merit-and-demerit evaluation and that their guilt should be fixed first, without mixing the matter into the regular evaluation.

sentences.zh: 御史任贊化以劾體仁謫，甡論救，而力詆王永光媚珰，請罷黜。

translations.literal: Censor Ren Zanhua was banished for impeaching Tiren; Shen memorialized in his defense, and vigorously denounced Wang Yongguang for flattering the eunuchs, requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Ren Zanhua was banished for impeaching Tiren; Shen memorialized in his defense and vigorously denounced Wang Yongguang for currying favor with the eunuchs, requesting his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 皆不納。

translations.literal: None was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: None of his proposals was accepted.

sentences.zh: 出按河南。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to conduct an inspection tour of Henan.

sentences.zh: 妖人聚徒劫村落，甡遍捕賊魁誅之。

translations.literal: Sorcerers gathered followers and plundered villages; Shen everywhere captured the bandit chiefs and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When mystics gathered followers to raid villages, Shen tracked down the ringleaders throughout the region and had them put to death.

sentences.zh: 奉命振延綏饑，因諭散賊黨。

translations.literal: Received command to relieve famine in Yan-Sui; thereby admonished and dispersed the bandit cliques.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to provide famine relief in the Yan'an-Suide region, he took the occasion to persuade rebel bands to disband.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，即命按陜西。

translations.literal: The emperor heard; immediately ordered him to inspect Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he immediately appointed Shen to conduct an inspection tour of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 劾大將杜文煥冒功，置之法。

translations.literal: Impeached the great general Du Wenhuan for falsely claiming merit; placed him under the law.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the general Du Wenhuan for claiming credit he had not earned and had him punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 數為民請命，奏無不允。

translations.literal: Repeatedly pleaded on behalf of the people; memorials were never denied.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned on the people's behalf, and the emperor granted every request.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺丞，進左通政。

translations.literal: Transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review; promoted to left vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and promoted to left vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，超擢右僉都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: Seventh year, ninth month; extraordinarily promoted to right vice censor-in-chief; governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the seventh year (1634), he was abruptly promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 甡歷陳防禦、邊寇、練兵、恤民四難，及議兵、議將、議餉、議用人四事。

translations.literal: Shen in succession set forth four difficulties—defense, border bandits, training troops, succoring the people—and four matters for deliberation: troops, generals, pay, and employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Shen laid out in turn four pressing problems—defense, border raiders, military training, and relief for the people—and four topics for policy discussion: troop deployment, general selection, pay, and appointment of personnel.

sentences.zh: 每歲暮扼河防秦、豫賊，連三歲，無一賊潛渡，以閑修築邊墻。

translations.literal: Each year's end he blocked the river against Qin and Yu bandits; three years running, not one bandit secretly crossed; used the intervals to build border walls.
translations.idiomatic: Each winter he held the river line against bandits from Shaanxi and Henan; for three years running not a single raider slipped across, and in the intervals he built up the border fortifications.

sentences.zh: 八年四月上疏言：「晉民有三苦：一苦兇荒，無計糊口；

translations.literal: Eighth year, fourth month, he memorialized saying: "Shanxi people have three sufferings: first, suffering from famine and calamity, with no means to feed their mouths;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year (1635) he submitted a memorial: "The people of Shanxi endure three hardships: first, famine and disaster leave them no way to earn a living;

sentences.zh: 一苦追呼，無力輸租；

translations.literal: one, suffering from collection calls, with no strength to deliver rent;
translations.idiomatic: second, relentless tax demands when they have no means to pay their levies;

sentences.zh: 一苦殺掠，無策保全。

translations.literal: one, suffering from killing and plunder, with no stratagem to preserve their safety.
translations.idiomatic: third, raids and slaughter when they have no way to protect themselves.

sentences.zh: 由此悉為盜，請蠲最殘破地十州縣租。」

translations.literal: By this all became bandits; requested remission of rent for the ten prefectures and counties of the most ruined land."
translations.idiomatic: Driven to this, they have all turned bandit. I ask that grain taxes be remitted in the ten prefectures and counties worst devastated by the disorder."

sentences.zh: 帝即敕議行。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered the proposal debated and carried out.

sentences.zh: 戶部請稅間架，甡力爭，弗聽。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue requested a building-frame tax; Shen vigorously contested it; the court did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue proposed a tax on buildings, Shen fought it fiercely, but the court would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 其秋，我大清平察哈爾國，旋師略朔州，直抵忻、代，守將屢敗。

translations.literal: That autumn, Our Great Qing pacified the Chahar state; turned the army and raided Shuozhou; reached straight to Xin and Dai; defending generals were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Qing pacified Chahar; on the return march their army raided Shuozhou and swept toward Xinzhou and Daizhou, and the Ming defenders suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 總督楊嗣昌遣副將自代州往偵，亦敗走。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Yang Sichang sent a vice general from Daizhou to reconnoiter; he too was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Yang Sichang sent a vice general from Daizhou to reconnoiter; he too was beaten and driven off.

sentences.zh: 甡鐫五級，嗣昌及大同巡撫葉廷桂鐫三級，俱戴罪視事。

translations.literal: Shen was demoted five ranks; Sichang and Datong governor Ye Tinggui were demoted three ranks; all held office while wearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was demoted five ranks; Sichang and Ye Tinggui, governor of Datong, each lost three ranks; all three continued in office under censure.

sentences.zh: 先是，定襄縣地震者再，甡曰：「此必有東師也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Dingxiang County had earthquakes twice; Shen said: "This surely means an eastern army is coming."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dingxiang County had been shaken twice by earthquakes; Shen said, "This means an army is coming from the east."

sentences.zh: 飭有司繕守具，已而果入。

translations.literal: He ordered the officials to repair defense equipment; soon after they indeed entered.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the local officials to ready their defenses, and before long the enemy did indeed arrive.

sentences.zh: 定襄以有備，獨不被兵。

translations.literal: Dingxiang, because it had preparations, alone was not subjected to arms.
translations.idiomatic: Because it was prepared, Dingxiang alone escaped attack.

sentences.zh: 山西大盜賀宗漢、劉浩然、高加計皆前巡撫戴君恩所撫，擁眾自恣。

translations.literal: The great Shanxi bandits He Zonghan, Liu Haoran, and Gao Jiaji had all been pacified by the former governor Dai Jun'en; they held masses and indulged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The great Shanxi bandits He Zonghan, Liu Haoran, and Gao Jiaji had all been brought under nominal control by the previous governor Dai Jun'en and now lorded over their followers as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 甡陽為撫慰，而密令參將虎大威、劉光祚等圖之，以次皆被殲。

translations.literal: Shen outwardly pacified and comforted them, but secretly ordered Assistant Generals Hu Dawei, Liu Guangzuo, and others to scheme against them; in order all were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Shen offered them public reassurance while secretly ordering Assistant Generals Hu Dawei, Liu Guangzuo, and others to take them down; one after another they were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 甡行軍樹二白旗，脅從及老弱婦女跪其下，即免死，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Shen on campaign erected two white flags; coerced followers and the old, weak, and women knelt beneath them and were exempted from death; very many were fully preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign Shen raised two white flags; anyone who had been forced into the band and the old, weak, and women had only to kneel beneath them to be spared, and very many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 在晉四年，軍民戴若慈母。

translations.literal: In Jin four years, the military and civilians revered him as if a loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: During four years in Shanxi, soldiers and civilians alike revered him as they would a devoted mother.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，起兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, second month; recalled as left vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year (1638), he was recalled to serve as left vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 其冬，尚書楊嗣昌言邊關戒嚴，甡及添註侍郎惠世楊久不至，請改推。

translations.literal: That winter, Minister Yang Sichang said the border passes were on alert; Shen and the supplementary vice minister Hui Shiyang long did not arrive; he requested a change of nomination.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Minister Yang Sichang reported the border on high alert; Shen and the supplementary vice minister Hui Shiyang had long failed to report, and Yang asked that other candidates be nominated in their place.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，落職閑住。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; stripped of office and ordered to live in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and dismissed them from office to idle at home.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬起故官，明年命協理戎政。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, winter: recalled to his former office; the next year ordered to assist in managing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year (1640) he was restored to his former post; the following year he was ordered to assist in managing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問京營軍何以使練者盡精，汰者不嘩，甡對曰：「京營邊勇營萬二千專練騎射，壯丁二萬專練火器，廩給厚而技與散兵無異。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked how the capital garrison troops could make those trained all skilled while those culled did not clamor; Shen replied: "In the capital garrison, twelve thousand in the frontier-brave camp exclusively train mounted archery; twenty thousand stalwarts exclusively train firearms; grain pay is thick yet their skills are no different from ordinary troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked how the capital garrison could ensure that those who trained were all elite while those culled did not riot. Shen answered: "In the capital garrison, twelve thousand men in the frontier-brave corps train exclusively in mounted archery and twenty thousand stalwarts train in firearms alone, yet though their rations are generous their skills are no better than those of ordinary troops.

sentences.zh: 宜行分練法，技精者，散兵拔為邊勇，否則邊勇降為散兵，壯丁亦然。

translations.literal: One should implement a divided-training method: those skilled among ordinary troops should be promoted to frontier-brave status; otherwise frontier-brave men should be demoted to ordinary troops; stalwarts likewise.
translations.idiomatic: We should adopt a system of graded training: skilled ordinary soldiers should be promoted into the frontier-brave corps, and unskilled frontier-brave men demoted to ordinary rank—and the same for the firearms trainees.

sentences.zh: 老弱者汰補，革弊當以漸，不可使知有汰兵意。」

translations.literal: The old and weak should be culled and replenished; reforming abuses should be gradual; one cannot let them know there is intent to cull troops."
translations.idiomatic: The old and weak should be winnowed out and replaced gradually; reform must come step by step, without letting the men know they are being purged."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this plan.

sentences.zh: 又問別立戰營，能得堪戰者五萬否，甡對：「京營兵合堪戰。

translations.literal: He again asked whether separately establishing a battle camp could obtain fifty thousand fit for battle; Shen replied: "The capital garrison troops altogether are fit for battle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked whether setting up a separate battle corps could yield fifty thousand men ready to fight. Shen answered: "Taken together, the capital garrison already contains enough soldiers fit for combat.

sentences.zh: 承平日久，發兵剿賊，輒沿途雇充。

translations.literal: Long days of peace; when issuing troops to suppress bandits, they always hired fill-ins along the route.
translations.idiomatic: After so many years of peace, whenever troops are sent to suppress bandits, they are hired along the march to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 將領利月餉，遊民利剽敓，歸營則本軍復充伍。

translations.literal: Generals profit from monthly pay; vagrants profit from plunder; return to camp and the original army again fills the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Officers profit from the monthly stipends, vagabonds from the chance to plunder, and when the campaign ends the original garrison simply fills the ranks again.

sentences.zh: 今練兵法要在選將，有戰將自有戰兵，五萬非難。

translations.literal: Now the method of training troops lies in selecting generals; with battle generals one naturally has battle troops; fifty thousand is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The key to drill today is choosing the right commanders; with good generals come good soldiers, and fifty thousand is not hard to raise.

sentences.zh: 但法忌紛更，不必別立戰營也。」

translations.literal: But methods dread frequent changes; there is no need separately to establish a battle camp."
translations.idiomatic: But policy should avoid constant upheaval—there is no need to create a separate battle corps."

sentences.zh: 帝顧兵部尚書陳新甲，令速選將，而諭甡具疏以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor looked at War Minister Chen Xinjia, ordered swift selection of generals, and instructed Shen to prepare a memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to War Minister Chen Xinjia and ordered a rapid search for commanders, then told Shen to submit a detailed memorial.

sentences.zh: 賜果餌，拜謝出。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed fruit and cakes; Shen bowed in thanks and went out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him fruit and confections; Shen bowed in thanks and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月，擢禮部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, sixth month; promoted to Minister of Rites concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year (1642), he was promoted to Minister of Rites and appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 周延儒再相，馮銓力為多，延儒許復其冠帶。

translations.literal: Zhou Yanru again became chancellor; Feng Quan exerted much effort; Yanru promised to restore his cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yanru returned as chief grand secretary, Feng Quan lobbied hard on his behalf, and Yanru promised to restore his official standing.

sentences.zh: 銓果以捐資振饑屬撫按題敘，延儒擬優旨下戶部。

translations.literal: Quan indeed took donating funds for famine relief and had the governor-censor memorialize for reward; Yanru drafted a favorable edict to send to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan had a record of famine relief donations entered for commendation by the provincial governor and censor, and Yanru drafted a favorable edict for the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 公議大沸，延儒患之。

translations.literal: Public opinion greatly boiled; Yanru worried.
translations.idiomatic: Public outrage erupted, and Yanru grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 馮元飆為甡謀，說延儒引甡共為銓地，延儒默援之，甡遂得柄用。

translations.literal: Feng Yuanbiao schemed for Shen; persuaded Yanru to draw Shen in to jointly make ground for Quan; Yanru silently assisted; Shen thus obtained power and employment.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yuanbiao devised a plan for Shen, persuading Yanru to bring Shen in to help smooth Feng Quan's path; Yanru quietly backed it, and Shen thus gained real influence at court.

sentences.zh: 及延儒語銓事，甡唯唯，退召戶部尚書傅淑訓，告以逆案不可翻，寢其疏不覆。

translations.literal: When Yanru spoke of Quan's matter, Shen assented; withdrew and summoned Revenue Minister Fu Shuxun; told him the treason case could not be overturned; shelved the memorial without reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanru raised Feng Quan's case, Shen murmured agreement—but on retiring he summoned Revenue Minister Fu Shuxun, told him the treason conviction could not be reversed, and let the memorial die without response.

sentences.zh: 延儒始悟為甡紿。

translations.literal: Yanru first understood he had been deceived by Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Yanru realize Shen had outmaneuvered him.

sentences.zh: 延儒欲起張捷為南京右都御史，甡力尼之。

translations.literal: Yanru wished to raise Zhang Jie as right censor-in-chief at Nanjing; Shen vigorously obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru wanted to appoint Zhang Jie right censor-in-chief at Nanjing, but Shen blocked it resolutely.

sentences.zh: 甡居江北，延儒居江南，各樹黨。

translations.literal: Shen dwelt north of the river, Yanru south of the river; each established factions.
translations.idiomatic: Shen held sway north of the Yangzi and Yanru south of it, and each built a faction.

sentences.zh: 延儒引用錦衣都督駱養性，甡持不可。

translations.literal: Yanru promoted Embroidered Uniform Guard commander Luo Yangxing; Shen maintained it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru sought to promote the Embroidered Uniform Guard commander Luo Yangxing, but Shen objected.

sentences.zh: 後帝論諸司弊竇，甡言錦衣尤甚，延儒亦言緹騎之害，帝並納之。

translations.literal: Later the emperor discussed the corruption holes of the various departments; Shen said the Embroidered Uniform Guard was especially severe; Yanru also spoke of the harm of the mounted agents; the emperor accepted both.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor reviewed abuses across the ministries, Shen said the Guard was worst of all and Yanru likewise denounced the harm done by its mounted agents; the emperor accepted both criticisms.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月，帝以襄陽、荊州、承天連陷，召對廷臣，隕涕謂甡曰：「卿向歷巖疆，可往督湖廣師。」

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, third month; because Xiangyang, Jingzhou, and Chengtian fell in succession, the emperor summoned the court ministers for audience; falling tears, said to Shen: "You formerly traversed frontier posts; you may go supervise the Huguang army."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixteenth year (1643), after Xiangyang, Jingzhou, and Chengtian fell in succession, the emperor summoned the court, wept, and told Shen: "You have served on the frontiers—go and take command of the army in Huguang."

sentences.zh: 甡具疏請得精兵三萬，自金陵趨武昌，扼賊南下。

translations.literal: Shen fully memorialized, requesting to obtain elite troops of thirty thousand; from Jinling rush to Wuchang; block the bandits' southward advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shen submitted a detailed memorial asking for thirty thousand picked troops, proposing to march from Nanjing to Wuchang and block the rebels' drive south.

sentences.zh: 帝方念湖北，覽疏不悅，留中。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then thinking of Hubei; perused the memorial displeased; kept it at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, whose thoughts were fixed on Hubei, read the memorial with displeasure and shelved it.

sentences.zh: 甡請面對，帝御昭文閣，諭以所需兵多，猝難集。

translations.literal: Shen requested a face-to-face audience; the emperor attended at the Zhaowen Pavilion; instructed him that the needed troops were many and suddenly hard to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Shen asked for a personal audience; the emperor received him at the Zhaowen Pavilion and explained that the troops he wanted were too many to assemble on short notice.

sentences.zh: 南京隔遠，不必退守。

translations.literal: Nanjing was separated far away; there was no need to fall back and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing lay far away—there was no need to fall back and defend it.

sentences.zh: 甡奏：「左良玉跋扈甚，督師嗣昌九檄征兵，一旅不發。

translations.literal: Shen memorialized: "Zuo Liangyu is extremely domineering; Supervising General Sichang nine times edict-summoned troops, not one company sent.
translations.idiomatic: Shen replied: "Zuo Liangyu is wildly insubordinate; when Grand Coordinator Sichang sent nine orders for troops, he did not dispatch a single company.

sentences.zh: 臣不如嗣昌，而良玉踞江、漢甚於曩時，臣節制不行，徒損威重。

translations.literal: This minister is not equal to Sichang; yet Liangyu occupies the Jiang and Han more than formerly; this minister's control is not enforced; in vain damages authority and weight.
translations.idiomatic: I am no match for Sichang, yet Liangyu holds the Yangzi and Han even more arrogantly than before; my orders will not be obeyed, and my authority will only be diminished.

sentences.zh: 南京從襄陽順流下，窺伺甚易，宜兼顧，非退守。」

translations.literal: Nanjing from Xiangyang along the current downstream—spying is very easy; one should attend to both; this is not falling back to defend."
translations.idiomatic: From Xiangyang the rebels could slide downriver toward Nanjing all too easily—we must guard both fronts, not treat this as a retreat to the south."

sentences.zh: 大學士陳演言：「督師出，則督、撫兵皆其兵。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Chen Yan said: "When the supervising general goes out, then the governors' and coordinators' troops all are his troops."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Yan said, "When the supreme commander takes the field, the troops of every governor and coordinator become his to command."

sentences.zh: 甡言：「臣請兵，正為督、撫無兵耳。

translations.literal: Shen said: "This minister requests troops, precisely because the governors and coordinators have no troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shen answered, "I am asking for troops precisely because the governors and coordinators have none of their own.

sentences.zh: 使臣束手待賊，事機一失，有不忍言者。」

translations.literal: If this minister waits empty-handed for the bandits, once the opportunity is lost, there are things unbearable to speak of."
translations.idiomatic: If I must face the rebels empty-handed, one lost chance may bring consequences too terrible to name."

sentences.zh: 帝乃令兵部速議發兵。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the Ministry of War swiftly to deliberate on dispatching troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Ministry of War to decide quickly on dispatching troops.

sentences.zh: 尚書張國維請以總兵唐通、馬科及京營兵共一萬畀甡，又言此兵方北征，俟敵退始可調。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Guowei requested that commanders Tang Tong and Ma Ke together with capital garrison troops totaling ten thousand be given to Shen; also said these troops were just then on a northern expedition; wait until the enemy retreated before they could be transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Guowei proposed giving Shen ten thousand men under the commanders Tang Tong and Ma Ke along with capital garrison troops, but added that these units were on the northern front and could not be moved until the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝命姑俟之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered to wait for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him to wait for now.

sentences.zh: 甡屢請，帝曰：「徐之，敵退兵自集，卿獨往何益？」

translations.literal: Shen repeatedly requested; the emperor said: "Take it slowly; when the enemy retreats the troops will naturally gather; you alone going—what benefit?"
translations.idiomatic: Shen pressed repeatedly, but the emperor said, "Be patient—when the enemy pulls back the troops will come together. What good will it do for you to go alone?"

sentences.zh: 逾月，延儒出督師，朝受命，夕啟行。

translations.literal: After a month, Yanru went out as supervising general; at court received appointment, in the evening set out.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Yanru left as supreme commander—appointed in the morning and on the road that same evening.

sentences.zh: 蔣德璟謂倪元璐曰：「上欲吳公速行，緩言相慰者，試之耳，觀首輔疾趨可見。」

translations.literal: Jiang Dejing said to Ni Yuanlu: "The emperor wants Duke Wu to go swiftly; slow words to comfort him are only a test; observe the chief minister's hurried departure and it is visible."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dejing told Ni Yuanlu, "When the emperor tells Lord Wu to hurry while soothing him with delays, he is testing him—watch how quickly the chief minister departed and you will see."

sentences.zh: 甡卒遲回不肯行。

translations.literal: Shen finally hesitated and refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shen hung back and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 部所撥唐通兵，演又請留，雲關門不可無備。

translations.literal: The Ministry-allocated Tang Tong troops—Chen Yan again requested to retain them, saying the pass gates could not be without defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan then asked to keep the Tang Tong detachment the Ministry had assigned, arguing the passes could not be left undefended.

sentences.zh: 甡不得已，以五月辭朝。

translations.literal: Shen had no choice; in the fifth month took leave of court.
translations.idiomatic: At last, in the fifth month, Shen bowed out of court and prepared to depart.

sentences.zh: 先一日出勞從騎，帝猶命中官賜銀牌給賞，越宿忽下詔責其逗遛，命輟行入直。

translations.literal: One day before, he went out to encourage the escort riders; the emperor still ordered eunuchs to bestow silver plaques as reward; overnight suddenly issued an edict rebuking his delay; ordered him to halt the journey and enter duty at court.
translations.idiomatic: The day before he set out he reviewed his escort; the emperor even sent eunuchs with silver tokens as a reward—but overnight an edict condemned his stalling and ordered him to stop and resume duty at court.

sentences.zh: 甡惶恐，兩疏引罪，遂許致仕。

translations.literal: Shen was fearful; twice memorialized accepting guilt; then was permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, stricken with fear, twice submitted memorials admitting fault and was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 既行，演及駱養性交構之，帝益怒。

translations.literal: After he departed, Chen Yan and Luo Yangxing slandered him together; the emperor grew more angry.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, Chen Yan and Luo Yangxing whispered against him, and the emperor's anger deepened.

sentences.zh: 至七月，親鞫吳昌時，作色曰：「兩輔臣負朕，朕待延儒厚，乃納賄行私，罔知國法。

translations.literal: By the seventh month, while personally trying Wu Changshi, he changed color and said: "The two assistant ministers betrayed Us; We treated Yanru generously; yet he took bribes and pursued private ends, ignorant of state law.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, while personally interrogating Wu Changshi, the emperor flushed with rage and said, "Both chief ministers have betrayed me. I treated Yanru generously, yet he took bribes and pursued private ends with no regard for the law.

sentences.zh: 命甡督師，百方延緩，為委卸地。

translations.literal: Ordered Shen to supervise the army; in a hundred ways delayed; made ground for shirking.
translations.idiomatic: When I ordered Shen to take command, he found every excuse to delay and leave himself a way out.

sentences.zh: 延儒被糾，甡何獨無？」

translations.literal: Yanru is being impeached; why is Shen alone without it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanru is being prosecuted—why is Shen exempt?"

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「朕雖言，終必無糾者，錦衣衛可宣甡候旨。」

translations.literal: Then again he said: "Although We speak, in the end surely none will impeach; the Embroidered Uniform Guard may summon Shen to await the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Then he added, "Words are one thing—no one will actually prosecute him. Let the Embroidered Uniform Guard summon Shen and hold him for instructions."

sentences.zh: 甡入都，敕法司議罪。

translations.literal: Shen entered the capital; ordered the judicial offices to deliberate on guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen reached the capital, the emperor ordered the legal authorities to determine his punishment.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣戍金齒。

translations.literal: Eleventh month; sent to exile at Jinchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was banished to Jinchi.

sentences.zh: 南京兵部尚書史可法馳疏救，不從。

translations.literal: Nanjing War Minister Shi Kefa rushed a memorial to rescue him; the emperor did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing War Minister Shi Kefa sent an urgent memorial in his defense, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，行次南康，聞都城變。

translations.literal: The next year, on the journey stopped at Nankang; heard the capital city had changed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, while passing through Nankang, he heard that the capital had fallen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，福王立於南京，赦還，復故秩。

translations.literal: Before long, Prince Fu was established at Nanjing; amnesty and return; restored to former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Prince Fu was enthroned at Nanjing; Shen was pardoned, recalled, and restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張慎言議召用甡，為勛臣劉孔昭等所阻。

translations.literal: Personnel Minister Zhang Shenyan deliberated summoning and employing Shen; blocked by meritorious ministers Liu Kongzhao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel Minister Zhang Shenyan proposed calling Shen back into service, but meritorious nobles led by Liu Kongzhao blocked it.

sentences.zh: 國變後，久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After the national change, long after, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Long after the dynasty's collapse, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明季士大夫問錢谷不知，問甲兵不知，於是嗣昌得以才顯。

translations.literal: Praise says: In the late Ming, scholar-officials asked about revenue and grain and knew not; asked about armor and troops and knew not; thereby Sichang by talent became prominent.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In the late Ming, literati who knew nothing of finance or supplies and nothing of arms and armies were the rule—and so Sichang rose on talent alone.

sentences.zh: 然迄無成功者，得非功罪淆於愛憎，機宜失於遙制故耶？

translations.literal: Yet to the end none succeeded; could it not be that merit and guilt were confused in love and hate, and opportune measures were lost in remote control?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end none of them succeeded—was it not because merit and blame were warped by favor and spite, and because command from afar squandered every chance?

sentences.zh: 吳甡按山右有聲，及為相，遂不能有為。

translations.literal: Wu Shen, inspecting right mountain, had reputation; when he became chancellor, then could not achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen won renown as censor of Shanxi, yet once he became chief minister he could accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 進不以正，其能正邦乎？

translations.literal: Advance not by the correct path; how can he correct the state?
translations.idiomatic: If a man rises to power by unworthy means, how can he set the realm right?

sentences.zh: 抑時勢實難，非命世材，固罔知攸濟也。

translations.literal: Yet the times' situation was truly difficult; without a world-ordering talent, one would surely not know how to deliver relief.
translations.idiomatic: Or perhaps the age was simply too hard—even one not born to save the world could hardly have known how.
